     * Updates our representation of the global namespace to reflect an
     * assignment to a global name in global scope.
     *
     * @param t The traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")

     *     assignment of the form <code>a.b.c = ...;</code>
     * @param type The type of the value that the name is being assigned

Method code:
544 |     void handleSetFromGlobal(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent, String name,
545 |                              boolean isPropAssign, Name.Type type) {

547 | 
548 |       Name nameObj = getOrCreateName(name);
549 |       nameObj.type = type;
550 | 
551 |       Ref set = new Ref(t, n, nameObj, Ref.Type.SET_FROM_GLOBAL,
552 |           currentPreOrderIndex++);

   * Traverses a branch.

476 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
477 |   private void traverseBranch(Node n, Node parent) {
478 |     int type = n.getType();
479 |     if (type == Token.SCRIPT) {
480 |       inputId = n.getInputId();
481 |       sourceName = getSourceName(n);
482 |     }
483 | 
484 |     curNode = n;
485 |     if (!callback.shouldTraverse(this, n, parent)) return;
486 | 
487 |     switch (type) {
488 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
489 |         traverseFunction(n, parent);
490 |         break;
491 | 
492 |       default:

494 |           // child could be replaced, in which case our child node

496 |           Node next = child.getNext();
497 |           traverseBranch(child, n);

501 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.java
Original range: 105-156
Documentation:

Method code:
105 |   @Override
106 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
107 | 
108 |     switch (n.getType()) {
109 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
110 |         {
111 |           // Add recursive function name, if needed.
112 |           // NOTE: "enterScope" is called after we need to pick up this name.
113 |           Renamer renamer = nameStack.peek().forChildScope();
114 | 
115 |           // If needed, add the function recursive name.
116 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
117 |           if (name != null && !name.isEmpty() && parent != null
118 |               && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
119 |             renamer.addDeclaredName(name);
120 |           }
121 | 
122 |           nameStack.push(renamer);
123 |         }
124 |         break;
125 | 
126 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST: {
127 |           Renamer renamer = nameStack.peek().forChildScope();
128 | 
129 |           // Add the function parameters
130 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
131 |             String name = c.getString();
132 |             renamer.addDeclaredName(name);
133 |           }
134 | 
135 |           // Add the function body declarations
136 |           Node functionBody = n.getNext();
137 |           findDeclaredNames(functionBody, null, renamer);
138 | 
139 |           nameStack.push(renamer);
140 |         }
141 |         break;
142 | 
143 |       case Token.CATCH:
144 |         {
145 |           Renamer renamer = nameStack.peek().forChildScope();
146 | 
147 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
148 |           renamer.addDeclaredName(name);
149 | 
150 |           nameStack.push(renamer);
151 |         }
152 |         break;
153 |     }
154 | 
155 |     return true;
156 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocTokenStream.getJsDocToken()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocTokenStream.java
Original range: 58-194
Documentation:
/**
   * Tokenizes JSDoc comments.
   */
Method code:
58 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
59 |   final JsDocToken getJsDocToken() {
60 |     int c;
61 |     stringBufferTop = 0;
62 |     for (;;) {
63 |       // eat white spaces
64 |       for (;;) {
65 |         charno = -1;
66 |         c = getChar();
67 |         if (c == EOF_CHAR) {
68 |           return JsDocToken.EOF;
69 |         } else if (c == '\n') {
70 |           return JsDocToken.EOL;
71 |         } else if (!isJSSpace(c)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |       }
75 | 
76 |       switch (c) {
77 |         // annotation, e.g. @type or @constructor
78 |         case '@':
79 |           do {
80 |             c = getChar();
81 |             if (isAlpha(c)) {
82 |               addToString(c);
83 |             } else {
84 |               ungetChar(c);
85 |               this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
86 |               stringBufferTop = 0;
87 |               return JsDocToken.ANNOTATION;
88 |             }
89 |           } while (true);
90 | 
91 |         case '*':
92 |           if (matchChar('/')) {
93 |             return JsDocToken.EOC;
94 |           } else {
95 |             return JsDocToken.STAR;
96 |           }
97 | 
98 |         case ',':
99 |           return JsDocToken.COMMA;
100 | 
101 |         case '>':
102 |           return JsDocToken.GT;
103 | 
104 |         case '(':
105 |           return JsDocToken.LP;
106 | 
107 |         case ')':
108 |           return JsDocToken.RP;
109 | 
110 |         case '{':
111 |           return JsDocToken.LC;
112 | 
113 |         case '}':
114 |           return JsDocToken.RC;
115 | 
116 |         case '[':
117 |           return JsDocToken.LB;
118 | 
119 |         case ']':
120 |           return JsDocToken.RB;
121 | 
122 |         case '?':
123 |           return JsDocToken.QMARK;
124 | 
125 |         case '!':
126 |           return JsDocToken.BANG;
127 | 
128 |         case ':':
129 |           return JsDocToken.COLON;
130 | 
131 |         case '=':
132 |           return JsDocToken.EQUALS;
133 | 
134 |         case '|':
135 |           matchChar('|');
136 |           return JsDocToken.PIPE;
137 | 
138 |         case '.':
139 |           c = getChar();
140 |           if (c == '<') {
141 |             return JsDocToken.LT;
142 |           } else {
143 |             if (c == '.') {
144 |               c = getChar();
145 |               if (c == '.') {
146 |                 return JsDocToken.ELLIPSIS;
147 |               } else {
148 |                 addToString('.');
149 |               }
150 |             }
151 |             // we may backtrack across line boundary
152 |             ungetBuffer[ungetCursor++] = c;
153 |             c = '.';
154 |           }
155 |           // fall through
156 | 
157 |         default: {
158 |           // recognize a JsDoc string but discard last . if it is followed by
159 |           // a non-JsDoc comment char, e.g. Array.<
160 |           int c1 = c;
161 |           addToString(c);
162 |           int c2 = getChar();
163 |           if (!isJSDocString(c2)) {
164 |             ungetChar(c2);
165 |             this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
166 |             stringBufferTop = 0;
167 |             return JsDocToken.STRING;
168 |           } else {
169 |             do {
170 |               c1 = c2;
171 |               c2 = getChar();
172 |               if (c1 == '.' && c2 == '<') {
173 |                 ungetChar(c2);
174 |                 ungetChar(c1);
175 |                 this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
176 |                 stringBufferTop = 0;
177 |                 return JsDocToken.STRING;
178 |               } else {
179 |                 if (isJSDocString(c2)) {
180 |                   addToString(c1);
181 |                 } else {
182 |                   ungetChar(c2);
183 |                   addToString(c1);
184 |                   this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
185 |                   stringBufferTop = 0;
186 |                   return JsDocToken.STRING;
187 |                 }
188 |               }
189 |             } while (true);
190 |           }
191 |         }
192 |       }
193 |     }
194 |   }

===== M0058 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.traverseNode(Node,Node,Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 192-296
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced.
   *
   * During traversal, we identify subtrees that will only be
   * referenced if their enclosing variables are referenced. Instead of
   * traversing those subtrees, we create a continuation for them,
   * and traverse them lazily.
   */
Method code:
192 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
193 |     int type = n.getType();
194 |     Var var = null;
195 |     switch (type) {
196 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
197 |         // If this function is a removable var, then create a continuation
198 |         // for it instead of traversing immediately.
199 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
200 |           var = scope.getVar(n.getFirstChild().getString());
201 |         }
202 | 
203 |         if (var != null && isRemovableVar(var)) {
204 |           continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
205 |         } else {
206 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
207 |         }
208 |         return;
209 | 
210 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
211 |         Assign maybeAssign = Assign.maybeCreateAssign(n);
212 |         if (maybeAssign != null) {
213 |           // Put this in the assign map. It might count as a reference,
214 |           // but we won't know that until we have an index of all assigns.
215 |           var = scope.getVar(maybeAssign.nameNode.getString());
216 |           if (var != null) {
217 |             assignsByVar.put(var, maybeAssign);
218 |             assignsByNode.put(maybeAssign.nameNode, maybeAssign);
219 | 
220 |             if (isRemovableVar(var) &&
221 |                 !maybeAssign.mayHaveSecondarySideEffects) {
222 |               // If the var is unreferenced and performing this assign has
223 |               // no secondary side effects, then we can create a continuation
224 |               // for it instead of traversing immediately.
225 |               continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
226 |               return;
227 |             }
228 |           }
229 |         }
230 |         break;
231 | 
232 |       case Token.CALL:
233 |         // Look for calls to inheritance-defining calls (such as goog.inherits).
234 |         SubclassRelationship subclassRelationship =
235 |             codingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(n);
236 |         if (subclassRelationship != null) {
237 |           Var subclassVar = scope.getVar(subclassRelationship.subclassName);
238 |           // Don't try to track the inheritance calls for non-globals. It would
239 |           // be more correct to only not track when the subclass does not
240 |           // reference a constructor, but checking that it is a global is
241 |           // easier and mostly the same.
242 |           if (subclassVar != null && subclassVar.isGlobal()
243 |               && !referenced.contains(subclassVar)) {
244 |             // Save a reference to the EXPR node.
245 |             inheritsCalls.put(subclassVar, parent);
246 |             continuations.put(subclassVar, new Continuation(n, scope));
247 |             return;
248 |           }
249 |         }
250 |         break;
251 | 
252 |       case Token.NAME:
253 |         var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
254 |         if (parent.isVar()) {
255 |           Node value = n.getFirstChild();
256 |           if (value != null && var != null && isRemovableVar(var) &&
257 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(value)) {
258 |             // If the var is unreferenced and creating its value has no side
259 |             // effects, then we can create a continuation for it instead
260 |             // of traversing immediately.
261 |             continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
262 |             return;
263 |           }
264 |         } else {
265 | 
266 |           // If arguments is escaped, we just assume the worst and continue
267 |           // on all the parameters.
268 |           if ("arguments".equals(n.getString()) && scope.isLocal()) {
269 |             Node lp = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
270 |             for (Node a = lp.getFirstChild(); a != null; a = a.getNext()) {
271 |               markReferencedVar(scope.getVar(a.getString()));
272 |             }
273 |           }
274 | 
275 |           // All name references that aren't declarations or assigns
276 |           // are references to other vars.
277 |           if (var != null) {
278 |             // If that var hasn't already been marked referenced, then
279 |             // start tracking it.  If this is an assign, do nothing
280 |             // for now.
281 |             if (isRemovableVar(var)) {
282 |               if (!assignsByNode.containsKey(n)) {
283 |                 markReferencedVar(var);
284 |               }
285 |             } else {
286 |               markReferencedVar(var);
287 |             }
288 |           }
289 |         }
290 |         break;
291 |     }
292 | 
293 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
294 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
295 |     }
296 |   }

===== M0061 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.isBlockBoundary(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 207-237
Documentation:
/**
   * @return true if this node marks the start of a new basic block
   */
Method code:
207 |   private static boolean isBlockBoundary(Node n, Node parent) {
208 |     if (parent != null) {
209 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
210 |         case Token.DO:
211 |         case Token.FOR:
212 |         case Token.TRY:
213 |         case Token.WHILE:
214 |         case Token.WITH:
215 |           // NOTE: TRY has up to 3 child blocks:
216 |           // TRY
217 |           //   BLOCK
218 |           //   BLOCK
219 |           //     CATCH
220 |           //   BLOCK
221 |           // Note that there is an explicit CATCH token but no explicit
222 |           // FINALLY token. For simplicity, we consider each BLOCK
223 |           // a separate basic BLOCK.
224 |           return true;
225 |         case Token.AND:
226 |         case Token.HOOK:
227 |         case Token.IF:
228 |         case Token.OR:
229 |           // The first child of a conditional is not a boundary,
230 |           // but all the rest of the children are.
231 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
232 | 
233 |       }
234 |     }
235 | 
236 |     return n.isCase();
237 |   }

43 |       case Token.ASSIGN:

45 |       case Token.COMMA:
46 |         return tryFoldComma(subtree);
47 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
48 |       case Token.BLOCK:
49 |         return tryOptimizeBlock(subtree);
50 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
51 |         subtree = tryFoldExpr(subtree);
52 |         return subtree;
53 |       case Token.HOOK:
54 |         return tryFoldHook(subtree);
55 |       case Token.SWITCH:
56 |         return tryOptimizeSwitch(subtree);
57 |       case Token.IF:
58 |         return tryFoldIf(subtree);
59 |       case Token.WHILE:
60 |         return tryFoldWhile(subtree);
61 |        case Token.FOR: {
62 |           Node condition = NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(subtree);
63 |           if (condition != null) {
64 |             tryFoldForCondition(condition);
65 |           }
66 |         }
67 |         return tryFoldFor(subtree);
68 |       case Token.DO:
69 |         return tryFoldDo(subtree);
70 |       case Token.TRY:
71 |         return tryFoldTry(subtree);
72 |       default:
73 |           return subtree;
74 |     }
75 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 493-534
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempt to replace the condition of if or hook immediately that is a
   * reference to a name that is assigned immediately before.
   */
Method code:
493 |   private void tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node n) {
494 |     Node next = n.getNext();
495 | 
496 |     // Look for patterns like the following and replace the if-condition with
497 |     // a constant value so it can later be folded:
498 |     //   var a = /a/;
499 |     //   if (a) {foo(a)}
500 |     // or
501 |     //   a = 0;
502 |     //   a ? foo(a) : c;
503 |     // or
504 |     //   a = 0;
505 |     //   a || foo(a);
506 |     // or
507 |     //   a = 0;
508 |     //   a && foo(a)
509 |     //
510 |     // TODO(johnlenz): This would be better handled by control-flow sensitive
511 |     // constant propagation. As the other case that I want to handle is:
512 |     //   i=0; for(;i<0;i++){}
513 |     // as right now nothing facilitates removing a loop like that.
514 |     // This is here simply to remove the cruft left behind goog.userAgent and
515 |     // similar cases.
516 | 
517 |     if (isSimpleAssignment(n) && isConditionalStatement(next)) {
518 |       Node lhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentName(n);
519 | 
520 |       Node condition = getConditionalStatementCondition(next);
521 |       if (lhsAssign.isName() && condition.isName()
522 |           && lhsAssign.getString().equals(condition.getString())) {
523 |         Node rhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentValue(n);
524 |         TernaryValue value = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(rhsAssign);
525 |         if (value != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
526 |           Node replacementConditionNode =
527 |               NodeUtil.booleanNode(value.toBoolean(true));
528 |           condition.getParent().replaceChild(condition,
529 |               replacementConditionNode);
530 |           reportCodeChange();
531 |         }
532 |       }
533 |     }
534 |   }

===== M0121 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 76-116
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a expression. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function.
   * Note: unlike getBooleanValue this function does not return UNKNOWN
   * for expressions with side-effects.
   */
Method code:
76 |   static TernaryValue getImpureBooleanValue(Node n) {
77 |     switch (n.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
79 |       case Token.COMMA:
80 |         // For ASSIGN and COMMA the value is the value of the RHS.
81 |         return getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
82 |       case Token.NOT:
83 |         TernaryValue value = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
84 |         return value.not();
85 |       case Token.AND: {
86 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
87 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
88 |         return lhs.and(rhs);
89 |       }
90 |       case Token.OR:  {
91 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
92 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
93 |         return lhs.or(rhs);
94 |       }
95 |       case Token.HOOK:  {
96 |         TernaryValue trueValue = getImpureBooleanValue(
97 |             n.getFirstChild().getNext());
98 |         TernaryValue falseValue = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
99 |         if (trueValue.equals(falseValue)) {
100 |           return trueValue;
101 |         } else {
102 |           return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
103 |         }
104 |       }
105 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
106 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
107 |         // ignoring side-effects
108 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
109 | 
110 |       case Token.VOID:
111 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
112 | 
113 |       default:
114 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n);
115 |     }
116 |   }

===== M0135 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldAndOr(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java
Original range: 562-600
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to fold a AND/OR node.
   */
Method code:
562 |   private Node tryFoldAndOr(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
563 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
564 | 
565 |     Node result = null;
566 | 
567 |     int type = n.getType();
568 | 
569 |     TernaryValue leftVal = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(left);
570 | 
571 |     if (leftVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
572 |       boolean lval = leftVal.toBoolean(true);
573 | 
574 |       // (TRUE || x) => TRUE (also, (3 || x) => 3)
575 |       // (FALSE && x) => FALSE
576 |       if (lval && type == Token.OR ||
577 |           !lval && type == Token.AND) {
578 |         result = left;
579 | 
580 |       } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
581 |         // (FALSE || x) => x
582 |         // (TRUE && x) => x
583 |         result = right;
584 |       }
585 |     }
586 | 
587 |     // Note: Right hand side folding is handled by
588 |     // PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax#tryMinimizeCondition
589 | 
590 |     if (result != null) {
591 |       // Fold it!
592 |       n.removeChild(result);
593 |       parent.replaceChild(n, result);
594 |       reportCodeChange();
595 | 
596 |       return result;
597 |     } else {
598 |       return n;
599 |     }
600 |   }

===== M0201 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 586-623
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * the name a is not.
   *
   * Function literals do not meet this definition, because they
   * lexically capture variables. For example, if you have
   * <code>
   * function() { return a; }
   * </code>
   * If it is evaluated in a different scope, then it
   * captures a different variable. Even if the function did not read
   * any captured variables directly, it would still fail this definition,
   * because it affects the lifecycle of variables in the enclosing scope.
   *
   * However, a function literal with respect to a particular scope is
   * a literal.
   *
   * @param includeFunctions If true, all function expressions will be
   *     treated as literals.
   */
Method code:
586 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n, boolean includeFunctions) {
587 |     switch (n.getType()) {
588 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
589 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
590 |              child = child.getNext()) {
591 |           if ((!child.isEmpty()) && !isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
592 |             return false;
593 |           }
594 |         }
595 |         return true;
596 | 
597 |       case Token.REGEXP:
598 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
599 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
600 |              child = child.getNext()) {
601 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
602 |             return false;
603 |           }
604 |         }
605 |         return true;
606 | 
607 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
608 |         // Return true only if all values are const.
609 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
610 |              child = child.getNext()) {
611 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions)) {
612 |             return false;
613 |           }
614 |         }
615 |         return true;
616 | 
617 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
618 |         return includeFunctions && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n);
619 | 
620 |       default:
621 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
622 |     }
623 |   }

615 |   private Node tryFoldIf(Node n) {
616 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isIf());
617 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
618 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(parent);
619 |     int type = n.getType();
620 |     Node cond = n.getFirstChild();
621 |     Node thenBody = cond.getNext();
622 |     Node elseBody = thenBody.getNext();
623 | 
624 |     // if (x) { .. } else { } --> if (x) { ... }
625 |     if (elseBody != null && !mayHaveSideEffects(elseBody)) {
626 |       n.removeChild(elseBody);
627 |       elseBody = null;
628 |       reportCodeChange();
629 |     }
630 | 
631 |     // if (x) { } else { ... } --> if (!x) { ... }
632 |     if (!mayHaveSideEffects(thenBody) && elseBody != null) {
633 |       n.removeChild(elseBody);
634 |       n.replaceChild(thenBody, elseBody);
635 |       Node notCond = new Node(Token.NOT);
636 |       n.replaceChild(cond, notCond);
637 |       notCond.addChildToFront(cond);
638 |       cond = notCond;
639 |       thenBody = cond.getNext();
640 |       elseBody = null;
641 |       reportCodeChange();
642 |     }
643 | 
644 |     // if (x()) { }
645 |     if (!mayHaveSideEffects(thenBody) && elseBody == null) {
646 |       if (mayHaveSideEffects(cond)) {
647 |         // x() has side effects, just leave the condition on its own.
648 |         n.removeChild(cond);
649 |         Node replacement = NodeUtil.newExpr(cond);
650 |         parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
651 |         reportCodeChange();
652 |         return replacement;
653 |       } else {
654 |         // x() has no side effects, the whole tree is useless now.
655 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(parent, n);
656 |         reportCodeChange();
657 |         return null;
658 |       }
659 |     }
660 | 
661 |     // Try transforms that apply to both IF and HOOK.
662 |     TernaryValue condValue = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(cond);
663 |     if (condValue == TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
664 |       return n;  // We can't remove branches otherwise!
665 |     }
666 | 
667 |     if (mayHaveSideEffects(cond)) {
668 |       // Transform "if (a = 2) {x =2}" into "if (true) {a=2;x=2}"
669 |       boolean newConditionValue = condValue == TernaryValue.TRUE;
670 |       // Add an elseBody if it is needed.
671 |       if (!newConditionValue && elseBody == null) {
672 |         elseBody = IR.block().srcref(n);
673 |         n.addChildToBack(elseBody);
674 |       }
675 |       Node newCond = NodeUtil.booleanNode(newConditionValue);
676 |       n.replaceChild(cond, newCond);
677 |       Node branchToKeep = newConditionValue ? thenBody : elseBody;
678 |       branchToKeep.addChildToFront(IR.exprResult(cond).srcref(cond));
679 |       reportCodeChange();
680 |       cond = newCond;
681 |     }
682 | 
683 |     boolean condTrue = condValue.toBoolean(true);
684 |     if (n.getChildCount() == 2) {
685 |       Preconditions.checkState(type == Token.IF);
686 | 
687 |       if (condTrue) {
688 |         // Replace "if (true) { X }" with "X".
689 |         Node thenStmt = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
690 |         n.removeChild(thenStmt);
691 |         parent.replaceChild(n, thenStmt);
692 |         reportCodeChange();
693 |         return thenStmt;
694 |       } else {
695 |         // Remove "if (false) { X }" completely.
696 |         NodeUtil.redeclareVarsInsideBranch(n);
697 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(parent, n);
698 |         reportCodeChange();
699 |         return null;
700 |       }
701 |     } else {
702 |       // Replace "if (true) { X } else { Y }" with X, or
703 |       // replace "if (false) { X } else { Y }" with Y.
704 |       Node trueBranch = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
705 |       Node falseBranch = trueBranch.getNext();
706 |       Node branchToKeep = condTrue ? trueBranch : falseBranch;
707 |       Node branchToRemove = condTrue ? falseBranch : trueBranch;
708 |       NodeUtil.redeclareVarsInsideBranch(branchToRemove);
709 |       n.removeChild(branchToKeep);
710 |       parent.replaceChild(n, branchToKeep);
711 |       reportCodeChange();
712 |       return branchToKeep;
713 |     }
714 |   }

/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
125 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
126 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
127 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
128 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
129 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
130 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
131 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
132 | 
133 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
134 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
135 |         }
136 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
137 |       } else {
138 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
139 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 | 
143 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
144 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
145 |     }
146 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 151-197
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
151 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
152 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
153 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.BLOCK:
155 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
156 |       case Token.TRY:
157 |         return true;
158 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
159 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
160 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
161 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
162 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
163 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
164 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
165 |         // child.
166 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
167 |       case Token.WHILE:
168 |       case Token.DO:
169 |       case Token.IF:
170 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
171 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
172 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.FOR:
175 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
176 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
177 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
178 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
179 |         // That way the following:
180 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
181 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
182 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
183 |           // TODO(user): Investigate how we should handle the case where
184 |           // we have a very complex expression inside the FOR-IN header.
185 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
186 |         } else {
187 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
188 |         }
189 |       case Token.SWITCH:
190 |       case Token.CASE:
191 |       case Token.CATCH:
192 |       case Token.WITH:
193 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
194 |       default:
195 |         return false;
196 |     }
197 |   }

/**
   * Try turning IF nodes into smaller HOOKs
   *
   * Returns the replacement for n or the original if no replacement was
   * necessary.

Method code:
627 |   private Node tryMinimizeIf(Node n) {
628 | 
629 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
630 | 
631 |     Node cond = n.getFirstChild();
632 | 
633 |     /* If the condition is a literal, we'll let other
634 |      * optimizations try to remove useless code.
635 |      */
636 |     if (NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(cond, true)) {
637 |       return n;
638 |     }
639 | 
640 |     Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
641 |     Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
642 | 
643 |     if (elseBranch == null) {
644 |       if (isFoldableExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
645 |         Node expr = getBlockExpression(thenBranch);
646 |         if (!late && isPropertyAssignmentInExpression(expr)) {
647 |           // Keep opportunities for CollapseProperties such as
648 |           // a.longIdentifier || a.longIdentifier = ... -> var a = ...;
649 |           // until CollapseProperties has been run.
650 |           return n;
651 |         }
652 | 
653 |         if (cond.isNot()) {
654 |           // if(!x)bar(); -> x||bar();
655 |           if (isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(cond, OR_PRECEDENCE) &&
656 |               isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(expr.getFirstChild(),
657 |                   OR_PRECEDENCE)) {
658 |             // It's not okay to add two sets of parentheses.
659 |             return n;
660 |           }
661 | 
662 |           Node or = IR.or(
663 |               cond.removeFirstChild(),
664 |               expr.removeFirstChild()).srcref(n);
665 |           Node newExpr = NodeUtil.newExpr(or);
666 |           parent.replaceChild(n, newExpr);
667 |           reportCodeChange();
668 | 
669 |           return newExpr;
670 |         }
671 | 
672 |         // if(x)foo(); -> x&&foo();
673 |         if (isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(cond, AND_PRECEDENCE) &&
674 |             isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(expr.getFirstChild(),
675 |                 AND_PRECEDENCE)) {
676 |           // One additional set of parentheses is worth the change even if
677 |           // there is no immediate code size win. However, two extra pair of
678 |           // {}, we would have to think twice. (unless we know for sure the
679 |           // we can further optimize its parent.
680 |           return n;
681 |         }
682 | 
683 |         n.removeChild(cond);
684 |         Node and = IR.and(cond, expr.removeFirstChild()).srcref(n);
685 |         Node newExpr = NodeUtil.newExpr(and);
686 |         parent.replaceChild(n, newExpr);
687 |         reportCodeChange();
688 | 
689 |         return newExpr;
690 |       } else {
691 | 
692 |         // Try to combine two IF-ELSE
693 |         if (NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(thenBranch) &&
694 |             thenBranch.hasOneChild()) {
695 |           Node innerIf = thenBranch.getFirstChild();
696 | 
697 |           if (innerIf.isIf()) {
698 |             Node innerCond = innerIf.getFirstChild();
699 |             Node innerThenBranch = innerCond.getNext();
700 |             Node innerElseBranch = innerThenBranch.getNext();
701 | 
702 |             if (innerElseBranch == null &&
703 |                  !(isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(cond, AND_PRECEDENCE) &&
704 |                    isLowerPrecedenceInExpression(innerCond, AND_PRECEDENCE))) {
705 |               n.detachChildren();
706 |               n.addChildToBack(
707 |                   IR.and(
708 |                       cond,
709 |                       innerCond.detachFromParent())
710 |                       .srcref(cond));
711 |               n.addChildrenToBack(innerThenBranch.detachFromParent());
712 |               reportCodeChange();
713 |               // Not worth trying to fold the current IF-ELSE into && because
714 |               // the inner IF-ELSE wasn't able to be folded into && anyways.
715 |               return n;
716 |             }
717 |           }
718 |         }
719 |       }
720 | 
721 |       return n;
722 |     }
723 | 
724 |     /* TODO(dcc) This modifies the siblings of n, which is undesirable for a
725 |      * peephole optimization. This should probably get moved to another pass.
726 |      */
727 |     tryRemoveRepeatedStatements(n);
728 | 
729 |     // if(!x)foo();else bar(); -> if(x)bar();else foo();
730 |     // An additional set of curly braces isn't worth it.
731 |     if (cond.isNot() && !consumesDanglingElse(elseBranch)) {
732 |       n.replaceChild(cond, cond.removeFirstChild());
733 |       n.removeChild(thenBranch);
734 |       n.addChildToBack(thenBranch);
735 |       reportCodeChange();
736 |       return n;
737 |     }
738 | 
739 |     // if(x)return 1;else return 2; -> return x?1:2;
740 |     if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpressBlock(elseBranch)) {
741 |       Node thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
742 |       Node elseExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(elseBranch);
743 |       n.removeChild(cond);
744 |       thenExpr.detachFromParent();
745 |       elseExpr.detachFromParent();
746 | 
747 |       // note - we ignore any cases with "return;", technically this
748 |       // can be converted to "return undefined;" or some variant, but
749 |       // that does not help code size.
750 |       Node returnNode = IR.returnNode(
751 |                             IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
752 |                                 .srcref(n));
753 |       parent.replaceChild(n, returnNode);
754 |       reportCodeChange();
755 |       return returnNode;
756 |     }
757 | 
758 |     boolean thenBranchIsExpressionBlock = isFoldableExpressBlock(thenBranch);
759 |     boolean elseBranchIsExpressionBlock = isFoldableExpressBlock(elseBranch);
760 | 
761 |     if (thenBranchIsExpressionBlock && elseBranchIsExpressionBlock) {
762 |       Node thenOp = getBlockExpression(thenBranch).getFirstChild();
763 |       Node elseOp = getBlockExpression(elseBranch).getFirstChild();
764 |       if (thenOp.getType() == elseOp.getType()) {
765 |         // if(x)a=1;else a=2; -> a=x?1:2;
766 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(thenOp)) {
767 |           Node lhs = thenOp.getFirstChild();
768 |           if (areNodesEqualForInlining(lhs, elseOp.getFirstChild()) &&
769 |               // if LHS has side effects, don't proceed [since the optimization
770 |               // evaluates LHS before cond]
771 |               // NOTE - there are some circumstances where we can
772 |               // proceed even if there are side effects...
773 |               !mayEffectMutableState(lhs)) {

786 |             reportCodeChange();

789 |           }

793 |       n.removeChild(cond);
794 |       thenOp.detachFromParent();
795 |       elseOp.detachFromParent();

797 |           IR.hook(cond, thenOp, elseOp).srcref(n));
798 |       parent.replaceChild(n, expr);
799 |       reportCodeChange();
800 |       return expr;
801 |     }
802 | 
803 |     boolean thenBranchIsVar = isVarBlock(thenBranch);
804 |     boolean elseBranchIsVar = isVarBlock(elseBranch);
805 | 
806 |     // if(x)var y=1;else y=2  ->  var y=x?1:2
807 |     if (thenBranchIsVar && elseBranchIsExpressionBlock &&

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceIf(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 297-368
Documentation:
/**
   * Use "return x?1:2;" in place of "if(x)return 1;return 2;"
   */
Method code:
297 |   private Node tryReplaceIf(Node n) {
298 | 
299 |     for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
300 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()){
301 |       if (child.isIf()){
302 |         Node cond = child.getFirstChild();
303 |         Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
304 |         Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
305 |         Node nextNode = child.getNext();
306 | 
307 |         if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null
308 |             && isReturnBlock(thenBranch)
309 |             && nextNode.isIf()) {
310 |           Node nextCond = nextNode.getFirstChild();
311 |           Node nextThen = nextCond.getNext();
312 |           Node nextElse = nextThen.getNext();
313 |           if (thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextThen)) {
314 |             // Transform
315 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) return 1;
316 |             // to
317 |             //   if (x||y) return 1;
318 |             child.detachFromParent();
319 |             child.detachChildren();
320 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.OR, cond);
321 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
322 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
323 |             reportCodeChange();
324 |           } else if (nextElse != null
325 |               && thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextElse)) {
326 |             // Transform
327 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) foo() else return 1;
328 |             // to
329 |             //   if (!x&&y) foo() else return 1;
330 |             child.detachFromParent();
331 |             child.detachChildren();
332 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.AND,
333 |                 IR.not(cond).srcref(cond));
334 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
335 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
336 |             reportCodeChange();
337 |           }
338 |         } else if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null &&
339 |             isReturnBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpression(nextNode)) {
340 |           Node thenExpr = null;
341 |           // if(x)return; return 1 -> return x?void 0:1
342 |           if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
343 |             thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
344 |             thenExpr.detachFromParent();
345 |           } else {
346 |             thenExpr = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(child);
347 |           }
348 | 
349 |           Node elseExpr = nextNode.getFirstChild();
350 | 
351 |           cond.detachFromParent();
352 |           elseExpr.detachFromParent();
353 | 
354 |           Node returnNode = IR.returnNode(
355 |                                 IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
356 |                                     .srcref(child));
357 |           n.replaceChild(child, returnNode);
358 |           n.removeChild(nextNode);
359 |           reportCodeChange();
360 |         } else if (elseBranch != null && statementMustExitParent(thenBranch)) {
361 |           child.removeChild(elseBranch);
362 |           n.addChildAfter(elseBranch, child);
363 |           reportCodeChange();
364 |         }
365 |       }
366 |     }
367 |     return n;
368 |   }

===== M0284 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.computeEscaped(Scope,Set<Var>,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 548-578
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in JavaScript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */
Method code:
548 |   static void computeEscaped(final Scope jsScope, final Set<Var> escaped,
549 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {
550 |     // TODO(user): Very good place to store this information somewhere.
551 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {
552 |       @Override
553 |       public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
554 |         if (jsScope == t.getScope() || !n.isName()
555 |             || parent.isFunction()) {
556 |           return;
557 |         }
558 |         String name = n.getString();
559 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
560 |         if (var != null && var.scope == jsScope) {
561 |           escaped.add(jsScope.getVar(name));
562 |         }
563 |       }
564 |     };
565 | 
566 |     NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, finder);
567 |     t.traverseAtScope(jsScope);
568 | 
569 |     // 1: Remove the exception name in CATCH which technically isn't local to
570 |     //    begin with.
571 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = jsScope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
572 |       Var var = i.next();
573 |       if (var.getParentNode().isCatch() ||
574 |           compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.getName())) {
575 |         escaped.add(var);
576 |       }
577 |     }
578 |   }

===== M0290 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 989-991
Documentation:
/**
   * Checks whether {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that}.<p>
   *
   * Subtyping rules:
   * <ul>
   * <li>(unknown) &mdash; every type is a subtype of the Unknown type.</li>
   * <li>(no) &mdash; the No type is a subtype of every type.</li>
   * <li>(no-object) &mdash; the NoObject type is a subtype of every object
   * type (i.e. subtypes of the Object type).</li>
   * <li>(ref) &mdash; a type is a subtype of itself.</li>
   * <li>(union-l) &mdash; A union type is a subtype of a type U if all the
   * union type's constituents are a subtype of U. Formally<br>
   * {@code (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>) &lt;: U} if and only
   * {@code T<sub>k</sub> &lt;: U} for all {@code k &isin; 1..n}.</li>
   * <li>(union-r) &mdash; A type U is a subtype of a union type if it is a
   * subtype of one of the union type's constituents. Formally<br>
   * {@code U &lt;: (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>)} if and only
   * if {@code U &lt;: T<sub>k</sub>} for some index {@code k}.</li>
   * <li>(objects) &mdash; an Object {@code O<sub>1</sub>} is a subtype
   * of an object {@code O<sub>2</sub>} if it has more properties
   * than {@code O<sub>2</sub>} and all common properties are
   * pairwise subtypes.</li>
   * </ul>
   *
   * @return {@code this &lt;: that}
   */
Method code:
989 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
990 |     return isSubtypeHelper(this, that);
991 |   }

70 |   @Override
71 |   public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
72 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
73 |     // Global scope _SHOULD_ work, however, liveness won't finish without
74 |     // -Xmx1024 in closure. We might have to look at coding conventions for
75 |     // exported variables as well.
76 |     if (scope.isGlobal()) {

86 |     // at least one inner function because in most browsers, when there is a

102 |     liveness = new LiveVariablesAnalysis(cfg, scope, compiler);

Original range: 409-422
Documentation:
/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in
     * var o = {'a' : 1, b: 2};
     * the string 'a' is quoted, while the name b is turned into a string, but
     * unquoted.
     */
Method code:
409 |     private Node transformAsString(AstNode n) {
410 |       Node ret;
411 |       if (n instanceof Name) {
412 |         ret = transformNameAsString((Name)n);
413 |       } else if (n instanceof NumberLiteral) {
414 |         ret = transformNumberAsString((NumberLiteral)n);
415 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
416 |       } else {
417 |         ret = transform(n);
418 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
419 |       }
420 |       Preconditions.checkState(ret.isString());
421 |       return ret;
422 |     }

/**
   * Initialize the compiler options. Only necessary if you're not doing
   * a normal compile() job.

Method code:
242 |   public void initOptions(CompilerOptions options) {
243 |     this.options = options;
244 |     if (errorManager == null) {

248 |       } else {

252 |         setErrorManager(printer);

292 |

967 |   private String jsString(String s, boolean useSlashV) {

===== M0337 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.addNonEmptyStatement(Node,Context,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 799-855
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds a block or expression, substituting a VOID with an empty statement.
   * This is used for "for (...);" and "if (...);" type statements.
   *
   * @param n The node to print.
   * @param context The context to determine how the node should be printed.
   */
Method code:
799 |   private void addNonEmptyStatement(
800 |       Node n, Context context, boolean allowNonBlockChild) {
801 |     Node nodeToProcess = n;
802 | 
803 |     if (!allowNonBlockChild && !n.isBlock()) {
804 |       throw new Error("Missing BLOCK child.");
805 |     }
806 | 
807 |     // Strip unneeded blocks, that is blocks with <2 children unless
808 |     // the CodePrinter specifically wants to keep them.
809 |     if (n.isBlock()) {
810 |       int count = getNonEmptyChildCount(n, 2);
811 |       if (count == 0) {
812 |         if (cc.shouldPreserveExtraBlocks()) {
813 |           cc.beginBlock();
814 |           cc.endBlock(cc.breakAfterBlockFor(n, context == Context.STATEMENT));
815 |         } else {
816 |           cc.endStatement(true);
817 |         }
818 |         return;
819 |       }
820 | 
821 |       if (count == 1) {
822 |         // Hack around a couple of browser bugs:
823 |         //   Safari needs a block around function declarations.
824 |         //   IE6/7 needs a block around DOs.
825 |         Node firstAndOnlyChild = getFirstNonEmptyChild(n);
826 |         boolean alwaysWrapInBlock = cc.shouldPreserveExtraBlocks();
827 |         if (alwaysWrapInBlock || isOneExactlyFunctionOrDo(firstAndOnlyChild)) {
828 |           cc.beginBlock();
829 |           add(firstAndOnlyChild, Context.STATEMENT);
830 |           cc.maybeLineBreak();
831 |           cc.endBlock(cc.breakAfterBlockFor(n, context == Context.STATEMENT));
832 |           return;
833 |         } else {
834 |           // Continue with the only child.
835 |           nodeToProcess = firstAndOnlyChild;
836 |         }
837 |       }
838 | 
839 |       if (count > 1) {
840 |         context = Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK;
841 |       }
842 |     }
843 | 
844 |     if (nodeToProcess.isEmpty()) {
845 |       cc.endStatement(true);
846 |     } else {
847 |       add(nodeToProcess, context);
848 | 
849 |       // VAR doesn't include ';' since it gets used in expressions - so any
850 |       // VAR in a statement context needs a call to endStatement() here.
851 |       if (nodeToProcess.isVar()) {
852 |         cc.endStatement();
853 |       }
854 |     }
855 |   }

===== M0355 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ExploitAssigns.collapseAssignEqualTo(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ExploitAssigns.java
Original range: 108-199
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse the given assign expression into the expression directly
   * following it, if possible.
   *
   * @param expr The expression that may be moved.
   * @param exprParent The parent of {@code expr}.
   * @param value The value of this expression, expressed as a node. Each
   *     expression may have multiple values, so this function may be called
   *     multiple times for the same expression. For example,
   *     <code>
   *     a = true;
   *     </code>
   *     is equal to the name "a" and the boolean "true".
   * @return Whether the expression was collapsed successfully.
   */
Method code:
108 |   private boolean collapseAssignEqualTo(Node expr, Node exprParent,
109 |       Node value) {
110 |     Node assign = expr.getFirstChild();
111 |     Node parent = exprParent;
112 |     Node next = expr.getNext();
113 |     while (next != null) {
114 |       switch (next.getType()) {
115 |         case Token.AND:
116 |         case Token.OR:
117 |         case Token.HOOK:
118 |         case Token.IF:
119 |         case Token.RETURN:
120 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
121 |           // Dive down the left side
122 |           parent = next;
123 |           next = next.getFirstChild();
124 |           break;
125 | 
126 |         case Token.VAR:
127 |           if (next.getFirstChild().hasChildren()) {
128 |             parent = next.getFirstChild();
129 |             next = parent.getFirstChild();
130 |             break;
131 |           }
132 |           return false;
133 | 
134 |         case Token.GETPROP:
135 |         case Token.NAME:
136 |           if (next.isQualifiedName()) {
137 |             String nextName = next.getQualifiedName();
138 |             if (value.isQualifiedName() &&
139 |                 nextName.equals(value.getQualifiedName())) {
140 |               // If the previous expression evaluates to value of a
141 |               // qualified name, and that qualified name is used again
142 |               // shortly, then we can exploit the assign here.
143 | 
144 |               // Verify the assignment doesn't change its own value.
145 |               if (!isSafeReplacement(next, assign)) {
146 |                 return false;
147 |               }
148 | 
149 |               exprParent.removeChild(expr);
150 |               expr.removeChild(assign);
151 |               parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
152 |               return true;
153 |             }
154 |           }
155 |           return false;
156 | 
157 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
158 |           // Assigns are really tricky. In lots of cases, we want to inline
159 |           // into the right side of the assign. But the left side of the
160 |           // assign is evaluated first, and it may have convoluted logic:
161 |           //   a = null;
162 |           //   (a = b).c = null;
163 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign. Similarly:
164 |           //   a.b = null;
165 |           //   a.b.c = null;
166 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign either.
167 |           //
168 |           // To protect against this, we simply only inline when the left side
169 |           // is guaranteed to evaluate to the same L-value no matter what.
170 |           Node leftSide = next.getFirstChild();
171 |           if (leftSide.isName() ||
172 |               leftSide.isGetProp() &&
173 |               leftSide.getFirstChild().isThis()) {
174 |             // Dive down the right side of the assign.
175 |             parent = next;
176 |             next = leftSide.getNext();
177 |             break;
178 |           } else {
179 |             return false;
180 |           }
181 | 
182 |         default:
183 |           if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(next)
184 |               && next.isEquivalentTo(value)) {
185 |             // If the r-value of the expr assign is an immutable value,
186 |             // and the value is used again shortly, then we can exploit
187 |             // the assign here.
188 |             exprParent.removeChild(expr);
189 |             expr.removeChild(assign);
190 |             parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
191 |             return true;
192 |           }
193 |           // Return without inlining a thing
194 |           return false;
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 | 
198 |     return false;
199 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ExploitAssigns.isCollapsibleValue(Node,boolean)

Original range: 76-91
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines whether we know enough about the given value to be able
   * to collapse it into subsequent expressions.
   *
   * For example, we can collapse booleans and variable names:
   * <code>
   * x = 3; y = x; // y = x = 3;
   * a = true; b = true; // b = a = true;
   * <code>
   * But we won't try to collapse complex expressions.
   *
   * @param value The value node.
   * @param isLValue Whether it's on the left-hand side of an expr.
   */
Method code:
76 |   private boolean isCollapsibleValue(Node value, boolean isLValue) {
77 |     switch (value.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.GETPROP:
79 |         // Do not collapse GETPROPs on arbitrary objects, because
80 |         // they may be implemented setter functions, and oftentimes
81 |         // setter functions fail on native objects. This is OK for "THIS"
82 |         // objects, because we assume that they are non-native.
83 |         return !isLValue || value.getFirstChild().isThis();
84 | 
85 |       case Token.NAME:
86 |         return true;
87 | 
88 |       default:
89 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value);
90 |     }
91 |   }

/**
   * Traverses a function.
   */
Method code:
510 |   private void traverseFunction(Node n, Node parent) {
511 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
512 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isFunction());
513 | 
514 |     final Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
515 | 
516 |     boolean isFunctionExpression = (parent != null)
517 |         && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n);
518 | 
519 |     if (!isFunctionExpression) {
520 |       // Functions declarations are in the scope containing the declaration.
521 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
522 |     }
523 | 
524 |     curNode = n;
525 |     pushScope(n);
526 | 
527 |     if (isFunctionExpression) {
528 |       // Function expression names are only accessible within the function
529 |       // scope.
530 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
531 |     }
532 | 
533 |     final Node args = fnName.getNext();
534 |     final Node body = args.getNext();
535 | 
536 |     // Args
537 |     traverseBranch(args, n);
538 | 
539 |     // Body
540 |     Preconditions.checkState(body.getNext() == null &&
541 |             body.isBlock(), body);
542 |     traverseBranch(body, n);
543 | 
544 |     popScope();
545 |   }

177 |     @Override
178 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
179 |       DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> graphNode = cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
180 |       if (graphNode == null) {
181 |         // Not a CFG node.

192 |           if (n.isName()) {
193 |

195 |             // node that gatherCb started at.
196 |             if (parent == null) {
197 |               return;
198 |             }
199 | 
200 |             // Make sure that the name node is purely a read.
201 |             if ((NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) && parent.getFirstChild() == n)
202 |                 || parent.isVar() || parent.isInc() || parent.isDec() ||

205 |             }

208 |             if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(name)) {
209 |               return;
210 |             }

213 |             // TODO(nicksantos): We need to add some notion of @const outer
214 |             // scope vars. We can inline those just fine.
215 |             if (defNode != null &&
216 |                 !reachingDef.dependsOnOuterScopeVars(name, cfgNode)) {
217 |               candidates.add(new Candidate(name, defNode, n, cfgNode));
218 |             }

   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If

Method code:
341 |   void setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType baseType, Node propertyNode) {
342 |     // This is a bit weird. We need to successfully handle these
343 |     // two cases:
344 |     // Foo.prototype = new Bar();
345 |     // and
346 |     // Foo.prototype = {baz: 3};
347 |     // In the first case, we do not want new properties to get
348 |     // added to Bar. In the second case, we do want new properties
349 |     // to get added to the type of the anonymous object.
350 |     //
351 |     // We handle this by breaking it into two cases:
352 |     //
353 |     // In the first case, we create a new PrototypeObjectType and set
354 |     // its implicit prototype to the type being assigned. This ensures
355 |     // that Bar will not get any properties of Foo.prototype, but properties
356 |     // later assigned to Bar will get inherited properly.
357 |     //
358 |     // In the second case, we just use the anonymous object as the prototype.
359 |     if (baseType.hasReferenceName() ||
360 |         isNativeObjectType() ||
361 |         baseType.isFunctionPrototypeType()) {
362 | 
363 |       baseType = new PrototypeObjectType(
364 |           registry, this.getReferenceName() + ".prototype", baseType);
365 |     }
366 |     setPrototype(baseType, propertyNode);

===== M0420 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 170-279
Documentation:
/**
   * General cascading unused operation node removal.
   * @param n The root of the expression to simplify.
   * @param removeUnused If true, the node is removed from the AST if
   *     it is not useful, otherwise it replaced with an EMPTY node.
   * @return The replacement node, or null if the node was is not useful.
   */
Method code:
170 |   private Node trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node n, boolean removeUnused) {
171 |     Node result = n;
172 | 
173 |     // Simplify the results of conditional expressions
174 |     switch (n.getType()) {
175 |       case Token.HOOK:
176 |         Node trueNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild().getNext());
177 |         Node falseNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
178 |         // If one or more of the conditional children were removed,
179 |         // transform the HOOK to an equivalent operation:
180 |         //    x() ? foo() : 1 --> x() && foo()
181 |         //    x() ? 1 : foo() --> x() || foo()
182 |         //    x() ? 1 : 1 --> x()
183 |         //    x ? 1 : 1 --> null
184 |         if (trueNode == null && falseNode != null) {
185 |           n.setType(Token.OR);
186 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
187 |         } else if (trueNode != null && falseNode == null) {
188 |           n.setType(Token.AND);
189 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
190 |         } else if (trueNode == null && falseNode == null) {
191 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
192 |         } else {
193 |           // The structure didn't change.
194 |           result = n;
195 |         }
196 |         break;
197 |       case Token.AND:
198 |       case Token.OR:
199 |         // Try to remove the second operand from a AND or OR operations:
200 |         //    x() || f --> x()
201 |         //    x() && f --> x()
202 |         Node conditionalResultNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(
203 |             n.getLastChild());
204 |         if (conditionalResultNode == null) {
205 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
206 |           // The conditionally executed code was removed, so
207 |           // replace the AND/OR with its LHS or remove it if it isn't useful.
208 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
209 |         }
210 |         break;
211 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
212 |         // A function expression isn't useful if it isn't used, remove it and
213 |         // don't bother to look at its children.
214 |         result = null;
215 |         break;
216 |       case Token.COMMA:
217 |         // We rewrite other operations as COMMA expressions (which will later
218 |         // get split into individual EXPR_RESULT statement, if possible), so
219 |         // we special case COMMA (we don't want to rewrite COMMAs as new COMMAs
220 |         // nodes.
221 |         Node left = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
222 |         Node right = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
223 |         if (left == null && right == null) {
224 |           result = null;
225 |         } else if (left == null) {
226 |           result = right;
227 |         } else if (right == null){
228 |           result = left;
229 |         } else {
230 |           // The structure didn't change.
231 |           result = n;
232 |         }
233 |         break;
234 |       default:
235 |         if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
236 |           // This is the meat of this function. The node itself doesn't generate
237 |           // any side-effects but preserve any side-effects in the children.
238 |           Node resultList = null;
239 |           for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
240 |             next = c.getNext();
241 |             c = trySimplifyUnusedResult(c);
242 |             if (c != null) {
243 |               c.detachFromParent();
244 |               if (resultList == null)  {
245 |                 // The first side-effect can be used stand-alone.
246 |                 resultList = c;
247 |               } else {
248 |                 // Leave the side-effects in-place, simplifying it to a COMMA
249 |                 // expression.
250 |                 resultList = IR.comma(resultList, c).srcref(c);
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |           result = resultList;
255 |         }
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // Fix up the AST, replace or remove the an unused node (if requested).
259 |     if (n != result) {
260 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
261 |       if (result == null) {
262 |         if (removeUnused) {
263 |           parent.removeChild(n);
264 |         } else {
265 |           result = IR.empty().srcref(n);
266 |           parent.replaceChild(n, result);
267 |         }
268 |       } else {
269 |         // A new COMMA expression may not have an existing parent.
270 |         if (result.getParent() != null) {
271 |           result.detachFromParent();
272 |         }
273 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, result);
274 |       }
275 |       reportCodeChange();
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     return result;
279 |   }

113 |   private void traverse(Node node) {
114 |     // The goal here is to avoid retraversing
115 |     // the entire AST to catch newly created opportunities.
116 |     // So we track whether a "unit of code" has changed,
117 |     // and revisit immediately.
118 |     if (!shouldVisit(node)) {
119 |       return;
120 |     }
121 | 
122 |     int visits = 0;
123 |     do {
124 |       for (Node c = node.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
125 |         traverse(c);
126 |       }
127 | 
128 |       visit(node);
129 |       visits++;
130 | 
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(visits < 10000, "too many interations");
132 |     } while (shouldRetraverse(node));
133 | 
134 |     exitNode(node);
135 |   }

/**
   * Looks for a type expression at the current token and if found,
   * returns it. Note that this method consumes input.
   *
   * Parameter type expressions are special for two reasons:
   * <ol>
   *   <li>They must begin with '{', to distinguish type names from param names.
   *   <li>They may end in '=', to denote optionality.
   * </ol>
   *
   * @param token The current token.
   * @return The type expression found or null if none.
   */
Method code:
1112 |   private Node parseAndRecordParamTypeNode(JsDocToken token) {
1113 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(token == JsDocToken.LC);
1114 |     int lineno = stream.getLineno();
1115 |     int startCharno = stream.getCharno();
1116 | 
1117 |     Node typeNode = parseParamTypeExpressionAnnotation(token);
1118 |     if (typeNode != null) {
1119 |       int endLineno = stream.getLineno();
1120 |       int endCharno = stream.getCharno();

38 |       return subtree;
39 |     }
40 | 
41 |     boolean codeChanged = false;
42 | 
43 |     // Look for variable declarations or simple assignments
44 |     // and start processing there.
45 |     for (Node child = subtree.getFirstChild();
46 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
47 |       if (!child.isVar() && !NodeUtil.isExprAssign(child)) {
48 |         continue;
49 |       }
50 |       if (!isPropertyAssignmentToName(child.getNext())) {
51 |         // Quick check to see if there's anything to collapse.
52 |         continue;
53 |       }
54 | 
55 |       Preconditions.checkState(child.hasOneChild());
56 |       Node name = getName(child);
57 |       if (!name.isName()) {
58 |         // The assignment target is not a simple name.
59 |         continue;
60 |       }
61 |       Node value = getValue(child);
62 |       if (value == null || !isInterestingValue(value)) {
63 |         // No initializer or not an Object or Array literal.
64 |         continue;
65 |       }
66 | 
67 |       Node propertyCandidate;
68 |       while ((propertyCandidate = child.getNext()) != null) {
69 |         // This does not infinitely loop because collectProperty always
70 |         // removes propertyCandidate from its parent when it returns true.
71 |         if (!collectProperty(propertyCandidate, name.getString(), value)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |         codeChanged = true;
75 |       }
76 |     }
77 |

79 |       reportCodeChange();
80 |     }

/**
     * Updates our representation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name's longest prefix before the "prototype" property if the
     * name includes the "prototype" property. Does nothing otherwise.
     *
     * @param t The current node traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return Whether the name was handled
     */
Method code:
781 |     boolean maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent,
782 |         String name) {
783 |       // We use a string-based approach instead of inspecting the parse tree
784 |       // to avoid complexities with object literals, possibly nested, beneath
785 |       // assignments.
786 | 
787 |       int numLevelsToRemove;
788 |       String prefix;
789 |       if (name.endsWith(".prototype")) {
790 |         numLevelsToRemove = 1;
791 |         prefix = name.substring(0, name.length() - 10);
792 |       } else {
793 |         int i = name.indexOf(".prototype.");
794 |         if (i == -1) {
795 |           return false;
796 |         }
797 |         prefix = name.substring(0, i);
798 |         numLevelsToRemove = 2;
799 |         i = name.indexOf('.', i + 11);
800 |         while (i >= 0) {
801 |           numLevelsToRemove++;
802 |           i = name.indexOf('.', i + 1);
803 |         }
804 |       }
805 | 
806 |       if (parent != null && NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
807 |         // Object literal keys have no prefix that's referenced directly per
808 |         // key, so we're done.
809 |         return true;
810 |       }
811 | 
812 |       for (int i = 0; i < numLevelsToRemove; i++) {
813 |         parent = n;
814 |         n = n.getFirstChild();
815 |       }
816 | 
817 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, prefix, Ref.Type.PROTOTYPE_GET);
818 |       return true;
819 |     }

===== M0463 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.UnreachableCodeElimination.tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/UnreachableCodeElimination.java
Original range: 130-179
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to remove n if an unconditional branch node (break, continue or
   * return) if the target of n is the same as the the follow of n. That is, if
   * we remove n, the control flow remains the same. Also if n targets to
   * another unconditional branch, this function will recursively try to remove
   * the target branch as well. The reason why we want to cascade this removal
   * is because we only run this pass once. If we have code such as
   *
   * break -> break -> break
   *
   * where all 3 break's are useless. The order of removal matters. When we
   * first look at the first break, we see that it branches to the 2nd break.
   * However, if we remove the last break, the 2nd break becomes useless and
   * finally the first break becomes useless as well.
   *
   * @return The target of this jump. If the target is also useless jump,
   *     the target of that useless jump recursively.
   */
Method code:
130 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
131 |   private Node tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node n) {
132 |     /*
133 |      * For each of the unconditional branching control flow node, check to see
134 |      * if the ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode of that node is same as
135 |      * the branching target. If it is, the branch node is safe to be removed.
136 |      *
137 |      * This is not as clever as MinimizeExitPoints because it doesn't do any
138 |      * if-else conversion but it handles more complicated switch statements
139 |      * much nicer.
140 |      */
141 | 
142 |     // If n is null the target is the end of the function, nothing to do.
143 |     if (n == null) {
144 |        return n;
145 |     }
146 | 
147 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = curCfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
148 | 
149 |     if (gNode == null) {
150 |       return n;
151 |     }
152 | 
153 |     switch (n.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.RETURN:
155 |         if (n.hasChildren()) {
156 |           break;
157 |         }
158 |       case Token.BREAK:
159 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
160 | 
161 |         // We are looking for a control flow changing statement that always
162 |         // branches to the same node. If removing it the control flow still
163 |         // branches to that same node. It is safe to remove it.
164 |         List<DiGraphEdge<Node,Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
165 |         if (outEdges.size() == 1 &&
166 |             // If there is a next node, there is no chance this jump is useless.
167 |             (n.getNext() == null || n.getNext().isFunction())) {
168 | 
169 |           Preconditions.checkState(outEdges.get(0).getValue() == Branch.UNCOND);
170 |           Node fallThrough = computeFollowing(n);
171 |           Node nextCfgNode = outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue();
172 |           if (nextCfgNode == fallThrough) {
173 |             removeDeadExprStatementSafely(n);
174 |             return fallThrough;
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 |     }
178 |     return n;
179 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MustBeReachingVariableDef.computeMustDef(Node,Node,MustDef,boolean)

Original range: 225-318

/**
   * @param n The node in question.
   * @param cfgNode The node to add
   * @param conditional true if the definition is not always executed.
   */
Method code:
225 |   private void computeMustDef(
226 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, MustDef output, boolean conditional) {
227 |     switch (n.getType()) {
228 | 
229 |       case Token.BLOCK:
230 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
231 |         return;
232 | 
233 |       case Token.WHILE:
234 |       case Token.DO:
235 |       case Token.IF:
236 |         computeMustDef(
237 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
238 |         return;
239 | 
240 |       case Token.FOR:
241 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
242 |           computeMustDef(
243 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
244 |         } else {
245 |           // for(x in y) {...}
246 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
247 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
248 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
249 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
250 |           }
251 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
252 |             addToDefIfLocal(lhs.getString(), cfgNode, rhs, output);
253 |           }
254 |         }
255 |         return;
256 | 
257 |       case Token.AND:
258 |       case Token.OR:
259 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
260 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
261 |         return;
262 | 
263 |       case Token.HOOK:
264 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
265 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
266 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
267 |         return;
268 | 
269 |       case Token.VAR:
270 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
271 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
272 |             computeMustDef(c.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
273 |             addToDefIfLocal(c.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
274 |                 c.getFirstChild(), output);
275 |           }
276 |         }
277 |         return;
278 | 
279 |       default:
280 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
281 |           if (n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
282 |             Node name = n.getFirstChild();
283 |             computeMustDef(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
284 |             addToDefIfLocal(name.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
285 |               n.getLastChild(), output);
286 |             return;
287 |           } else if (NodeUtil.isGet(n.getFirstChild())) {
288 |             // Treat all assignments to arguments as redefining the
289 |             // parameters itself.
290 |             Node obj = n.getFirstChild().getFirstChild();
291 |             if (obj.isName() && "arguments".equals(obj.getString())) {
292 |               // TODO(user): More accuracy can be introduced
293 |               // ie: We know exactly what arguments[x] is if x is a constant
294 |               // number.
295 |               escapeParameters(output);
296 |             }
297 |           }
298 |         }
299 | 
300 |         if (n.isName() && "arguments".equals(n.getString())) {
301 |           escapeParameters(output);
302 |         }
303 | 
304 |         // DEC and INC actually defines the variable.
305 |         if (n.isDec() || n.isInc()) {
306 |           Node target = n.getFirstChild();
307 |           if (target.isName()) {
308 |             addToDefIfLocal(target.getString(),
309 |                 conditional ? null : cfgNode, null, output);
310 |             return;
311 |           }
312 |         }
313 | 
314 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
315 |           computeMustDef(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
316 |         }
317 |     }
318 |   }
