/**
   * Finds all defines, and creates a {@link DefineInfo} data structure for
   * each one.
   * @return A map of {@link DefineInfo} structures, keyed by name.
   */
Method code:
172 |   private Map<String, DefineInfo> collectDefines(Node root,
173 |       GlobalNamespace namespace) {
174 |     // Find all the global names with a @define annotation
175 |     List<Name> allDefines = Lists.newArrayList();
176 |     for (Name name : namespace.getNameIndex().values()) {
177 |       Ref decl = name.getDeclaration();
178 |       if (name.docInfo != null && name.docInfo.isDefine()) {
179 |         // Process defines should not depend on check types being enabled,
180 |         // so we look for the JSDoc instead of the inferred type.
181 |         if (isValidDefineType(name.docInfo.getType())) {
182 |           allDefines.add(name);
183 |         } else {
184 |           JSError error = JSError.make(
185 |               decl.getSourceName(),
186 |               decl.node, INVALID_DEFINE_TYPE_ERROR);
187 |           compiler.report(error);
188 |         }
189 |       } else {
190 |         for (Ref ref : name.getRefs()) {
191 |           if (ref == decl) {
192 |             // Declarations were handled above.
193 |             continue;
194 |           }
195 | 
196 |           Node n = ref.node;
197 |           Node parent = ref.node.getParent();
198 |           JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
199 |           if (info == null &&
200 |               parent.isVar() && parent.hasOneChild()) {
201 |             info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
202 |           }
203 | 
204 |           if (info != null && info.isDefine()) {
205 |             allDefines.add(name);
206 |             break;
207 |           }
208 |         }
209 |       }
210 |     }
211 | 
212 |     CollectDefines pass = new CollectDefines(compiler, allDefines);
213 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, pass);
214 |     return pass.getAllDefines();
215 |   }

===== M0513 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.JSModuleGraph.manageDependencies(DependencyOptions,List<CompilerInput>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/JSModuleGraph.java
Original range: 311-390
Documentation:
/**
   * Apply the dependency options to the list of sources, returning a new
   * source list re-ordering and dropping files as necessary.
   * This module graph will be updated to reflect the new list.
   *
   * @param inputs The original list of sources. Used to ensure that the sort
   *     is stable.
   * @throws CircularDependencyException if there is a circular dependency
   *     between the provides and requires.
   * @throws MissingProvideException if an entry point was not provided
   *     by any of the inputs.
   * @see DependencyOptions for more info on how this works.
   */
Method code:
311 |   public List<CompilerInput> manageDependencies(
312 |       DependencyOptions depOptions,
313 |       List<CompilerInput> inputs)
314 |       throws CircularDependencyException, MissingProvideException {
315 | 
316 |     SortedDependencies<CompilerInput> sorter =
317 |         new SortedDependencies<CompilerInput>(inputs);
318 |     Set<CompilerInput> entryPointInputs = Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
319 |     if (depOptions.shouldPruneDependencies()) {
320 |       if (!depOptions.shouldDropMoochers()) {
321 |         entryPointInputs.addAll(sorter.getInputsWithoutProvides());
322 |       }
323 | 
324 |       for (String entryPoint : depOptions.getEntryPoints()) {
325 |         entryPointInputs.add(sorter.getInputProviding(entryPoint));
326 |       }
327 | 
328 |       CompilerInput baseJs = sorter.maybeGetInputProviding("goog");
329 |       if (baseJs != null) {
330 |         entryPointInputs.add(baseJs);
331 |       }
332 |     } else {
333 |       entryPointInputs.addAll(inputs);
334 |     }
335 | 
336 |     // The order of inputs, sorted independently of modules.
337 |     List<CompilerInput> absoluteOrder =
338 |         sorter.getDependenciesOf(inputs, depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
339 | 
340 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module.
341 |     ListMultimap<JSModule, CompilerInput> entryPointInputsPerModule =
342 |         LinkedListMultimap.create();
343 |     for (CompilerInput input : entryPointInputs) {
344 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
345 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(module);
346 |       entryPointInputsPerModule.put(module, input);
347 |     }
348 | 
349 |     // Clear the modules of their inputs. This also nulls out
350 |     // the input's reference to its module.
351 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
352 |       module.removeAll();
353 |     }
354 | 
355 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module, or in one
356 |     // of that module's dependencies.
357 |     for (JSModule module : entryPointInputsPerModule.keySet()) {
358 |       List<CompilerInput> transitiveClosure =
359 |           sorter.getDependenciesOf(
360 |               entryPointInputsPerModule.get(module),
361 |               depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
362 |       for (CompilerInput input : transitiveClosure) {
363 |         JSModule oldModule = input.getModule();
364 |         if (oldModule == null) {
365 |           input.setModule(module);
366 |         } else {
367 |           input.setModule(null);
368 |           input.setModule(
369 |               getDeepestCommonDependencyInclusive(oldModule, module));
370 |         }
371 |       }
372 |     }
373 | 
374 |     // All the inputs are pointing to the modules that own them. Yeah!
375 |     // Update the modules to reflect this.
376 |     for (CompilerInput input : absoluteOrder) {
377 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
378 |       if (module != null) {
379 |         module.add(input);
380 |       }
381 |     }
382 | 
383 |     // Now, generate the sorted result.
384 |     List<CompilerInput> result = Lists.newArrayList();
385 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
386 |       result.addAll(module.getInputs());
387 |     }
388 | 
389 |     return result;
390 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 124-170
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function
   * except it return UNKNOWN for known values with side-effects, use
   * getExpressionBooleanValue if you don't care about side-effects.
   */
Method code:
124 |   static TernaryValue getPureBooleanValue(Node n) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.STRING:
127 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getString().length() > 0);
128 | 
129 |       case Token.NUMBER:
130 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getDouble() != 0);
131 | 
132 |       case Token.NOT:
133 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild()).not();
134 | 
135 |       case Token.NULL:
136 |       case Token.FALSE:
137 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
138 | 
139 |       case Token.VOID:
140 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n.getFirstChild())) {
141 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
142 |         }
143 |         break;
144 | 
145 |       case Token.NAME:
146 |         String name = n.getString();
147 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
148 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
149 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
150 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
151 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
152 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
153 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
154 |         }
155 |         break;
156 | 
157 |       case Token.TRUE:
158 |       case Token.REGEXP:
159 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
160 | 
161 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
162 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
163 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
164 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
165 |         }
166 |         break;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
170 |   }

1513 |     }

52 |   public CheckLevel level(JSError error) {
53 |     Node node = error.node;
54 |     if (node != null) {
55 |       for (Node current = node;
56 |            current != null;
57 |            current = current.getParent()) {
58 |         int type = current.getType();
59 |         JSDocInfo info = null;
60 | 
61 |         // We only care about function annotations at the FUNCTION and SCRIPT
62 |         // level. Otherwise, the @suppress annotation has an implicit
63 |         // dependency on the exact structure of our AST, and that seems like
64 |         // a bad idea.
65 |         if (type == Token.FUNCTION) {
66 |           info = NodeUtil.getFunctionJSDocInfo(current);
67 |         } else if (type == Token.SCRIPT) {
68 |           info = current.getJSDocInfo();
69 |         } else if (type == Token.ASSIGN) {
70 |           Node rhs = current.getLastChild();
71 |           if (rhs.isFunction()) {
72 |             info = NodeUtil.getFunctionJSDocInfo(rhs);
73 |           }
74 |         }
75 | 
76 |         if (info != null) {
77 |           for (String suppressor : info.getSuppressions()) {
78 |             WarningsGuard guard = suppressors.get(suppressor);
79 | 
80 |             // Some @suppress tags are for other tools, and
81 |             // may not have a warnings guard.
82 |             if (guard != null) {
83 |               CheckLevel newLevel = guard.level(error);
84 |               if (newLevel != null) {
85 |                 return newLevel;
86 |               }
87 |             }
88 |           }
89 |         }
90 |       }
91 |     }
92 |     return null;
93 |   }

     * Split a var node such as:

524 |         // Shift the previous break to end of file by replacing it with a
525 |         // <space> and adding a new break at end of file. Adding the space
526 |         // handles cases like instanceof\nfoo. (it would be nice to avoid this)
527 |         code.setCharAt(prevCutPosition, ' ');
528 |         lineStartPosition = prevLineStartPosition;
529 |         lineLength = code.length() - lineStartPosition;
530 |         reportLineCut(lineIndex, prevCutPosition + 1, false);
531 |         lineIndex--;
532 |         prevCutPosition = 0;
533 |         prevLineStartPosition = 0;
534 |         append(";");
535 |         startNewLine();
536 |       } else {
537 |         // A small file with no line breaks. We do nothing in this case to
538 |         // avoid excessive line breaks. It's not ideal if a lot of these pile
539 |         // up, but that is reasonably unlikely.
540 |       }
541 |     }

   * Compare this node to node2 recursively and return the first pair of nodes
   * that differs doing a preorder depth-first traversal. Package private for
   * testing. Returns null if the nodes are equivalent.
   */

1444 |   NodeMismatch checkTreeEqualsImpl(Node node2) {

33 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
34 |     // if the operator is symmetric
35 |     if (NodeUtil.isSymmetricOperation(subtree)
36 |         || NodeUtil.isRelationalOperation(subtree)) {

49 |         Node lastNode = subtree.getLastChild().detachFromParent();

188 |     char c = newcode.charAt(0);
189 |     if ((isWordChar(c) || c == '\\') &&
190 |         isWordChar(getLastChar())) {
191 |       // need space to separate. This is not pretty printing.
192 |       // For example: "return foo;"
193 |       append(" ");
194 |     } else if (c == '/' && getLastChar() == '/') {
195 |       // Do not allow a forward slash to appear after a DIV.
196 |       // For example,
197 |       // REGEXP DIV REGEXP
198 |       // is valid and should print like
199 |       // / // / /
200 |       append(" ");
201 |     }
202 | 
203 |     append(newcode);
204 |   }

===== M0600 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.runCallable(Callable<T>,boolean,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 606-658
Documentation:

Method code:
606 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
607 |   static <T> T runCallable(
608 |       final Callable<T> callable, boolean useLargeStackThread, boolean trace) {
609 | 
610 |     // Under JRE 1.6, the JS Compiler overflows the stack when running on some
611 |     // large or complex JS code. Here we start a new thread with a larger
612 |     // stack in order to let the compiler do its thing, without having to
613 |     // increase the stack size for *every* thread (which is what -Xss does).
614 |     // Might want to add thread pool support for clients that compile a lot.
615 | 
616 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = trace;
617 |     final Object[] result = new Object[1];
618 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
619 |     Runnable runnable = new Runnable() {
620 |       @Override
621 |       public void run() {
622 |         try {
623 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
624 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
625 |           }
626 |           result[0] = callable.call();
627 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
628 |           exception[0] = e;
629 |         } finally {
630 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
631 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
632 |           }
633 |         }
634 |       }
635 |     };
636 | 
637 |     if (useLargeStackThread) {
638 |       Thread th = new Thread(null, runnable, "jscompiler", COMPILER_STACK_SIZE);
639 |       th.start();
640 |       while (true) {
641 |         try {
642 |           th.join();
643 |           break;
644 |         } catch (InterruptedException ignore) {
645 |           // ignore
646 |         }
647 |       }
648 |     } else {
649 |       runnable.run();
650 |     }
651 | 
652 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
653 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
654 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
655 |     }
656 | 
657 |     return (T) result[0];
658 |   }

===== M0603 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CommandLineRunner.processArgs(String[])
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CommandLineRunner.java
Original range: 601-627
Documentation:

Method code:
601 |   private List<String> processArgs(String[] args) {
602 |     // Args4j has a different format that the old command-line parser.
603 |     // So we use some voodoo to get the args into the format that args4j
604 |     // expects.
605 |     Pattern argPattern = Pattern.compile("(--[a-zA-Z_]+)=(.*)");
606 |     Pattern quotesPattern = Pattern.compile("^['\"](.*)['\"]$");
607 |     List<String> processedArgs = Lists.newArrayList();
608 | 
609 |     for (String arg : args) {
610 |       Matcher matcher = argPattern.matcher(arg);
611 |       if (matcher.matches()) {
612 |         processedArgs.add(matcher.group(1));
613 | 
614 |         String value = matcher.group(2);
615 |         Matcher quotesMatcher = quotesPattern.matcher(value);
616 |         if (quotesMatcher.matches()) {
617 |           processedArgs.add(quotesMatcher.group(1));
618 |         } else {
619 |           processedArgs.add(value);
620 |         }
621 |       } else {
622 |         processedArgs.add(arg);
623 |       }
624 |     }
625 | 
626 |     return processedArgs;
627 |   }

===== M0667 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

484 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
485 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
486 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
487 |     if (node.isBlock() && parent != null &&
488 |         parent.isTry() &&
489 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
490 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
491 |       return;
492 |     }
493 | 
494 |     // A block transfer control to its first child if it is not empty.
495 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();
496 | 
497 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that
498 |     // function (unless it is called)
499 |     while (child != null && child.isFunction()) {
500 |       child = child.getNext();
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     if (child != null) {
504 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFallThrough(child));
505 |     } else {
506 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFollowNode(node, this));
507 |     }
508 |

512 |         case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
513 |         case Token.CASE:
514 |         case Token.TRY:
515 |           break;
516 |         default:
517 |           if (node.isBlock() && node.isSyntheticBlock()) {
518 |             createEdge(node, Branch.SYN_BLOCK, computeFollowNode(node, this));

===== M0688 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 147-210
Documentation:

Method code:
147 |   @Override
148 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
149 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !n.isName() ||
150 |         parent.isFunction()) {
151 |       // Don't rename named functions.
152 |       return;
153 |     }
154 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
155 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
156 |     if (vNode == null) {
157 |       // This is not a local.
158 |       return;
159 |     }
160 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
161 | 
162 |     if (!usePseudoNames) {
163 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
164 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
165 |         return;
166 |       }
167 | 
168 |       // Rename.
169 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
170 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
171 | 
172 |       if (parent.isVar()) {
173 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
174 |       }
175 |     } else {
176 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
177 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
178 |       // make this fast.
179 |       String pseudoName = null;
180 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
181 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
182 |         Var iVar = i.next();
183 | 
184 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
185 |         // and it is merged with the current coalescedVar.
186 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
187 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
188 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
189 |         }
190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       // Keep its original name.
193 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
194 |         return;
195 |       }
196 | 
197 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
198 | 
199 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
200 |         pseudoName += "$";
201 |       }
202 | 
203 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
204 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
205 | 
206 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && parent.isVar()) {
207 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
208 |       }
209 |     }
210 |   }

/**
   * ParamTypeExpressionAnnotation :=
   *     '{' OptionalParameterType '}' |
   *     '{' TopLevelTypeExpression '}' |
   *     '{' '...' TopLevelTypeExpression '}'
   *
   * OptionalParameterType :=
   *     TopLevelTypeExpression '='
   */
Method code:
1569 |   private Node parseParamTypeExpressionAnnotation(JsDocToken token) {
1570 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(token == JsDocToken.LC);
1571 | 
1572 |     skipEOLs();
1573 | 
1574 |     boolean restArg = false;
1575 |     token = next();
1576 |     if (token == JsDocToken.ELLIPSIS) {
1577 |       token = next();
1578 |       if (token == JsDocToken.RC) {
1579 |         // EMPTY represents the UNKNOWN type in the Type AST.
1580 |         return wrapNode(Token.ELLIPSIS, IR.empty());
1581 |       }
1582 |       restArg = true;
1583 |     }

1585 |     Node typeNode = parseTopLevelTypeExpression(token);
1586 |     if (typeNode != null) {
1587 |       skipEOLs();
1588 |       if (restArg) {
1589 |         typeNode = wrapNode(Token.ELLIPSIS, typeNode);
1590 |       } else if (match(JsDocToken.EQUALS)) {
1591 |         next();
1592 |         skipEOLs();
1593 |         typeNode = wrapNode(Token.EQUALS, typeNode);
1594 |       }
1595 | 
1596 |       if (!match(JsDocToken.RC)) {
1597 |         reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.rc");
1598 |       } else {
1599 |         next();
1600 |       }
1601 |     }
1602 | 
1603 |     return typeNode;
1604 |   }

     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.
     *
     * For information on ES5 directives, see section 14.1 of
     * ECMA-262, Edition 5.
     *
     * It would be nice if Rhino would eventually take care of this for
     * us, but right now their directive-processing is a one-off.

175 |   @Override
176 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
177 |     switch (n.getType()) {
178 |       case Token.CALL:
179 |         boolean isExpr = parent.isExprResult();
180 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
181 |         if (left.isGetProp()) {
182 |           Node name = left.getFirstChild();
183 |           if (name.isName() &&
184 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
185 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
186 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
187 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
188 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
189 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
190 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
191 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
192 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
193 |               break;
194 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
195 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
196 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
197 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
198 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
199 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
200 |               if (arg.isString()) {
201 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
202 |                 if (dot == -1) {
203 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
204 |                 } else {
205 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
206 |                 }
207 |               }
208 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
209 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
210 |               List<String> typeDecls =
211 |                   convention.identifyTypeDeclarationCall(n);
212 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
213 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
214 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
215 |                 }
216 |               }
217 | 
218 |               // We can't modify parent, so just create a node that will
219 |               // get compiled out.
220 |               parent.replaceChild(n, IR.number(0));
221 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
222 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
223 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
224 |             }
225 |           }
226 |         }
227 |         break;
228 | 
229 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
230 |       case Token.NAME:
231 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
232 |         // object.
233 |         handleCandidateProvideDefinition(t, n, parent);
234 |         break;
235 | 
236 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
237 |         handleTypedefDefinition(t, n, parent);
238 |         break;
239 | 
240 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
241 |         // If this is a declaration of a provided named function, this is an
242 |         // error. Hoisted functions will explode if they're provided.
243 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&
244 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
245 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
246 |           ProvidedName pn = providedNames.get(name);
247 |           if (pn != null) {
248 |             compiler.report(t.makeError(n, FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_ERROR, name));
249 |           }
250 |         }
251 |         break;
252 |

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.collectProperty(Node,String,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.java
Original range: 130-169
Documentation:

Method code:
130 |   private boolean collectProperty(
131 |       Node propertyCandidate, String name, Node value) {
132 |     if (!isPropertyAssignmentToName(propertyCandidate)) {
133 |       return false;
134 |     }
135 | 
136 |     Node lhs = propertyCandidate.getFirstChild().getFirstChild();
137 |     // Must be an assignment to the recent variable...
138 |     if (!name.equals(lhs.getFirstChild().getString())) {
139 |       return false;
140 |     }
141 | 
142 |     Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
143 |     // with a value that cannot change the values of the variables,
144 |     if (NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(rhs)
145 |         || NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected(rhs)) {
146 |       return false;
147 |     }
148 |     // and does not have a reference to a variable initialized after it.
149 |     if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(rhs, true)
150 |         && mightContainForwardReference(rhs, name)) {
151 |       return false;
152 |     }
153 | 
154 |     switch (value.getType()) {
155 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
156 |         if (!collectArrayProperty(value, propertyCandidate)) {
157 |           return false;
158 |         }
159 |         break;
160 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
161 |         if (!collectObjectProperty(value, propertyCandidate)) {
162 |           return false;
163 |         }
164 |         break;
165 |       default:
166 |         throw new IllegalStateException();
167 |     }
168 |     return true;
169 |   }

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:
2401 |   static boolean isLatin(String s) {
2402 |     char LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN = 0x7f;
2403 |     int len = s.length();
2404 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
2405 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
2406 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
2407 |         return false;
2408 |       }
2409 |     }
2410 |     return true;
2411 |   }

Method code:
956 |   private static Map<String, Node> getReplacementsHelper(
957 |       Map<String, Object> source) {
958 |     Map<String, Node> map = Maps.newHashMap();
959 |     for (Map.Entry<String, Object> entry : source.entrySet()) {
960 |       String name = entry.getKey();
961 |       Object value = entry.getValue();
962 |       if (value instanceof Boolean) {

966 |       } else if (value instanceof Double) {
967 |         map.put(name, IR.number(((Double) value).doubleValue()));
968 |       } else {
969 |         Preconditions.checkState(value instanceof String);
970 |         map.put(name, IR.string((String) value));
971 |       }
972 |     }
973 |     return map;

===== M0771 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 785-929
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
785 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
786 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
787 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
788 |     // that we know to be safe
789 |     switch (n.getType()) {
790 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
791 |       case Token.AND:
792 |       case Token.BLOCK:
793 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
794 |       case Token.HOOK:
795 |       case Token.IF:
796 |       case Token.IN:
797 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
798 |       case Token.NUMBER:
799 |       case Token.OR:
800 |       case Token.THIS:
801 |       case Token.TRUE:
802 |       case Token.FALSE:
803 |       case Token.NULL:
804 |       case Token.STRING:
805 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
806 |       case Token.SWITCH:
807 |       case Token.TRY:
808 |       case Token.EMPTY:
809 |         break;
810 | 
811 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
812 |       case Token.THROW:
813 |         return true;
814 | 
815 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
816 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
817 |           return true;
818 |         }
819 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
820 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
821 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
822 |             return true;
823 |           }
824 |         }
825 |         return false;
826 | 
827 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
828 |       case Token.REGEXP:
829 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
830 |           return true;
831 |         }
832 |         break;
833 | 
834 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
835 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
836 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
837 |           return true;
838 |         }
839 |         break;
840 | 
841 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
842 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
843 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
844 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
845 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
846 | 
847 |       case Token.NEW:
848 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
849 |           return true;
850 |         }
851 | 
852 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
853 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
854 |           // side-effects
855 |           break;
856 |         }
857 |         return true;
858 | 
859 |       case Token.CALL:
860 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
861 |         // side effect property set.
862 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
863 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
864 |           // side-effects
865 |           break;
866 |         }
867 |         return true;
868 | 
869 |       default:
870 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType())) {
871 |           break;
872 |         }
873 | 
874 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
875 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
876 |           if (assignTarget.isName()) {
877 |             return true;
878 |           }
879 | 
880 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
881 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
882 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
883 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
884 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
885 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
886 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
887 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
888 |             return true;
889 |           }
890 | 
891 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
892 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
893 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
894 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
895 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
896 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
897 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
898 |               return false;
899 |             }
900 | 
901 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
902 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
903 |             // other objects.
904 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
905 |             // side-effect.
906 |             while (isGet(current)) {
907 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
908 |             }
909 | 
910 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
911 |           } else {
912 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
913 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
914 |             // preserve existing behavior.
915 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
916 |           }
917 |         }
918 | 
919 |         return true;
920 |     }
921 | 
922 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
923 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
924 |         return true;
925 |       }
926 |     }
927 | 
928 |     return false;
929 |   }

121 |     parseSucceeded = true;
122 | 
123 |     BufferedReader lineBuffer = new BufferedReader(fileContents);
124 | 
125 |     // Parse all lines.
126 |     String line = null;
127 |     lineNum = 0;
128 |     boolean inMultilineComment = false;
129 | 
130 |     try {
131 |       while (null != (line = lineBuffer.readLine())) {
132 |         ++lineNum;
133 |         try {
134 |           String revisedLine = line;
135 |           if (inMultilineComment) {
136 |             int endOfComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/");
137 |             if (endOfComment != -1) {
138 |               revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(endOfComment + 2);
139 |               inMultilineComment = false;
140 |             } else {
141 |               revisedLine = "";
142 |             }
143 |           }
144 | 
145 |           if (!inMultilineComment) {
146 |             while (true) {
147 |               int startOfLineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("//");
148 |               int startOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("/*");
149 |               if (startOfLineComment != -1 &&
150 |                   (startOfMultilineComment == -1 ||
151 |                    startOfLineComment < startOfMultilineComment)) {
152 |                 revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(0, startOfLineComment);
153 |                 break;
154 |               } else if (startOfMultilineComment != -1) {
155 |                 int endOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/",
156 |                     startOfMultilineComment + 2);
157 |                 if (endOfMultilineComment == -1) {
158 |                   revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(
159 |                       0, startOfMultilineComment);
160 |                   inMultilineComment = true;
161 |                   break;
162 |                 } else {
163 |                   revisedLine =
164 |                       revisedLine.substring(0, startOfMultilineComment) +
165 |                       revisedLine.substring(endOfMultilineComment + 2);
166 |                 }
167 |               } else {
168 |                 break;
169 |               }
170 |             }
171 |           }
172 | 
173 |           if (!revisedLine.isEmpty()) {
174 |             // This check for shortcut mode should be redundant, but
175 |             // it's done for safety reasons.
176 |             if (!parseLine(revisedLine) && shortcutMode) {
177 |               break;
178 |             }
179 |           }
180 |         } catch (ParseException e) {
181 |           // Inform the error handler of the exception.
182 |           errorManager.report(
183 |               e.isFatal() ? CheckLevel.ERROR : CheckLevel.WARNING,
184 |               JSError.make(filePath, lineNum, 0 /* char offset */,
185 |                   e.isFatal() ? PARSE_ERROR : PARSE_WARNING,
186 |                   e.getMessage(), line));
187 |           parseSucceeded = parseSucceeded && !e.isFatal();
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 |     } catch (IOException e) {
191 |       errorManager.report(CheckLevel.ERROR,
192 |           JSError.make(filePath, 0, 0 /* char offset */,
193 |               PARSE_ERROR, "Error reading file: " + filePath));
194 |       parseSucceeded = false;
195 |     }
196 |   }

/**
     * Updates our representation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name.
     *
     * @param t The traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     */
Method code:
643 |     void handleGet(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent, String name) {
644 |       if (maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(t, n, parent, name)) return;
645 | 
646 |       Ref.Type type = Ref.Type.DIRECT_GET;
647 |       if (parent != null) {
648 |         switch (parent.getType()) {
649 |           case Token.IF:
650 |           case Token.TYPEOF:
651 |           case Token.VOID:
652 |           case Token.NOT:
653 |           case Token.BITNOT:
654 |           case Token.POS:
655 |           case Token.NEG:
656 |             break;
657 |           case Token.CALL:
658 |             type = n == parent.getFirstChild()
659 |                    ? Ref.Type.CALL_GET
660 |                    : Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
661 |             break;
662 |           case Token.NEW:
663 |             type = n == parent.getFirstChild()
664 |                    ? Ref.Type.DIRECT_GET
665 |                    : Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
666 |             break;
667 |           case Token.OR:
668 |           case Token.AND:
669 |             // This node is x or y in (x||y) or (x&&y). We only know that an
670 |             // alias is not getting created for this name if the result is used
671 |             // in a boolean context or assigned to the same name
672 |             // (e.g. var a = a || {}).
673 |             type = determineGetTypeForHookOrBooleanExpr(t, parent, name);
674 |             break;
675 |           case Token.HOOK:
676 |             if (n != parent.getFirstChild()) {
677 |               // This node is y or z in (x?y:z). We only know that an alias is
678 |               // not getting created for this name if the result is assigned to
679 |               // the same name (e.g. var a = a ? a : {}).
680 |               type = determineGetTypeForHookOrBooleanExpr(t, parent, name);
681 |             }
682 |             break;
683 |           case Token.DELPROP:
684 |             type = Ref.Type.DELETE_PROP;
685 |             break;
686 |           default:
687 |             type = Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET;
688 |             break;
689 |         }
690 |       }
691 | 
692 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, name, type);
693 |     }

239 |   private static <T> List<T> topologicalStableSort(

258 |       }
259 |     });
260 |     List<T> result = Lists.newArrayList();
261 | 
262 |     Multiset<T> inDegree = HashMultiset.create();
263 |     Multimap<T, T> reverseDeps = ArrayListMultimap.create();
264 |     Multimaps.invertFrom(deps, reverseDeps);
265 | 
266 |     // First, add all the inputs with in-degree 0.
267 |     for (T item : items) {
268 |       Collection<T> itemDeps = deps.get(item);
269 |       inDegree.add(item, itemDeps.size());
270 |       if (itemDeps.isEmpty()) {
271 |         inDegreeZero.add(item);
272 |       }
273 |     }
274 | 
275 |     // Then, iterate to a fixed point over the reverse dependency graph.
276 |     while (!inDegreeZero.isEmpty()) {
277 |       T item = inDegreeZero.remove();
278 |       result.add(item);
279 |       for (T inWaiting : reverseDeps.get(item)) {
280 |         inDegree.remove(inWaiting, 1);
281 |         if (inDegree.count(inWaiting) == 0) {
282 |           inDegreeZero.add(inWaiting);
283 |         }
284 |       }
285 |     }
286 | 
287 |     return result;
288 |   }

===== M0834 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 704-753
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assignments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
704 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
705 |     boolean changes = false;
706 |     do {
707 |       changes = false;
708 | 
709 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
710 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
711 |       // we traverse it.
712 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
713 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
714 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
715 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
716 |           current--;
717 |         } else {
718 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
719 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
720 | 
721 |           if (var.getParentNode().isVar() &&
722 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
723 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
724 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
725 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
726 |           } else {
727 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
728 |             // or a for...in variable.
729 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
730 |           }
731 | 
732 |           boolean maybeEscaped = false;
733 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
734 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
735 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
736 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
737 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
738 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
739 |             }
740 |             if (assign.maybeAliased) {
741 |               maybeEscaped = true;
742 |             }
743 |           }
744 | 
745 |           if ((assignedToUnknownValue || maybeEscaped) && hasPropertyAssign) {
746 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
747 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
748 |             current--;
749 |           }
750 |         }
751 |       }
752 |     } while (changes);
753 |   }

===== M0850 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 560-607
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
560 |     private void extractForInitializer(
561 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
562 | 
563 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
564 |         next = c.getNext();
565 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
566 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
567 |         switch (c.getType()) {
568 |           case Token.LABEL:
569 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
570 |             break;
571 |           case Token.FOR:
572 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
573 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
574 |               if (first.isVar()) {
575 |                 // Transform:
576 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
577 |                 // to:
578 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
579 |                 Node newStatement = first;
580 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
581 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
582 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
583 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
584 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
585 |               }
586 |             } else if (!c.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
587 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
588 |               Node empty = IR.empty();
589 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
590 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
591 | 
592 |               Node newStatement;
593 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
594 |               // but are handled differently.
595 |               if (init.isVar()) {
596 |                 newStatement = init;
597 |               } else {
598 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
599 |               }
600 | 
601 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
602 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
603 |             }
604 |             break;
605 |         }
606 |       }
607 |     }

===== M0880 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.strEscape(String,char,String,String,String,CharsetEncoder,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 1016-1103
Documentation:
/** Helper to escape JavaScript string as well as regular expression */
Method code:
1016 |   private static String strEscape(
1017 |       String s, char quote,
1018 |       String doublequoteEscape,
1019 |       String singlequoteEscape,
1020 |       String backslashEscape,
1021 |       CharsetEncoder outputCharsetEncoder,
1022 |       boolean useSlashV) {
1023 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(s.length() + 2);
1024 |     sb.append(quote);
1025 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1026 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
1027 |       switch (c) {
1028 |         case '\0': sb.append("\\x00"); break;
1029 |         case '\u000B':
1030 |           if (useSlashV) {
1031 |             sb.append("\\v");
1032 |           } else {
1033 |             sb.append("\\x0B");
1034 |           }
1035 |           break;
1036 |         // From the SingleEscapeCharacter grammar production.
1037 |         case '\b': sb.append("\\b"); break;
1038 |         case '\f': sb.append("\\f"); break;
1039 |         case '\n': sb.append("\\n"); break;
1040 |         case '\r': sb.append("\\r"); break;
1041 |         case '\t': sb.append("\\t"); break;
1042 |         case '\\': sb.append(backslashEscape); break;
1043 |         case '\"': sb.append(doublequoteEscape); break;
1044 |         case '\'': sb.append(singlequoteEscape); break;
1045 | 
1046 |         // From LineTerminators (ES5 Section 7.3, Table 3)
1047 |         case '\u2028': sb.append("\\u2028"); break;
1048 |         case '\u2029': sb.append("\\u2029"); break;
1049 | 
1050 |         case '>':                       // Break --> into --\> or ]]> into ]]\>
1051 |           if (i >= 2 &&
1052 |               ((s.charAt(i - 1) == '-' && s.charAt(i - 2) == '-') ||
1053 |                (s.charAt(i - 1) == ']' && s.charAt(i - 2) == ']'))) {
1054 |             sb.append("\\>");
1055 |           } else {
1056 |             sb.append(c);
1057 |           }
1058 |           break;
1059 |         case '<':
1060 |           // Break </script into <\/script
1061 |           final String END_SCRIPT = "/script";
1062 | 
1063 |           // Break <!-- into <\!--
1064 |           final String START_COMMENT = "!--";
1065 | 
1066 |           if (s.regionMatches(true, i + 1, END_SCRIPT, 0,
1067 |                               END_SCRIPT.length())) {
1068 |             sb.append("<\\");
1069 |           } else if (s.regionMatches(false, i + 1, START_COMMENT, 0,
1070 |                                      START_COMMENT.length())) {
1071 |             sb.append("<\\");
1072 |           } else {
1073 |             sb.append(c);
1074 |           }
1075 |           break;
1076 |         default:
1077 |           // If we're given an outputCharsetEncoder, then check if the
1078 |           //  character can be represented in this character set.
1079 |           if (outputCharsetEncoder != null) {
1080 |             if (outputCharsetEncoder.canEncode(c)) {
1081 |               sb.append(c);
1082 |             } else {
1083 |               // Unicode-escape the character.
1084 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1085 |             }
1086 |           } else {
1087 |             // No charsetEncoder provided - pass straight Latin characters
1088 |             // through, and escape the rest.  Doing the explicit character
1089 |             // check is measurably faster than using the CharsetEncoder.
1090 |             if (c > 0x1f && c < 0x7f) {
1091 |               sb.append(c);
1092 |             } else {
1093 |               // Other characters can be misinterpreted by some JS parsers,
1094 |               // or perhaps mangled by proxies along the way,
1095 |               // so we play it safe and Unicode escape them.
1096 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1097 |             }
1098 |           }
1099 |       }
1100 |     }
1101 |     sb.append(quote);
1102 |     return sb.toString();
1103 |   }

===== M0889 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MaybeReachingVariableUse.computeMayUse(Node,Node,ReachingUses,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MaybeReachingVariableUse.java
Original range: 152-237
Documentation:

Method code:
152 |   private void computeMayUse(
153 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, ReachingUses output, boolean conditional) {
154 |     switch (n.getType()) {
155 | 
156 |       case Token.BLOCK:
157 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
158 |         return;
159 | 
160 |       case Token.NAME:
161 |         addToUseIfLocal(n.getString(), cfgNode, output);
162 |         return;
163 | 
164 |       case Token.WHILE:
165 |       case Token.DO:
166 |       case Token.IF:
167 |         computeMayUse(
168 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
169 |         return;
170 | 
171 |       case Token.FOR:
172 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
173 |           computeMayUse(
174 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
175 |         } else {
176 |           // for(x in y) {...}
177 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
178 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
179 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
180 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
181 |           }
182 |           if (lhs.isName() && !conditional) {
183 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(lhs.getString(), output);
184 |           }
185 |           computeMayUse(rhs, cfgNode, output, conditional);
186 |         }
187 |         return;
188 | 
189 |       case Token.AND:
190 |       case Token.OR:
191 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
192 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
193 |         return;
194 | 
195 |       case Token.HOOK:
196 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
197 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
198 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
199 |         return;
200 | 
201 |       case Token.VAR:
202 |         Node varName = n.getFirstChild();
203 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasChildren(), "AST should be normalized");
204 | 
205 |         if (varName.hasChildren()) {
206 |           computeMayUse(varName.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
207 |           if (!conditional) {
208 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(varName.getString(), output);
209 |           }
210 |         }
211 |         return;
212 | 
213 |       default:
214 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
215 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
216 |           if (!conditional) {
217 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(name.getString(), output);
218 |           }
219 | 
220 |           // In case of a += "Hello". There is a read of a.
221 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
222 |             addToUseIfLocal(name.getString(), cfgNode, output);
223 |           }
224 | 
225 |           computeMayUse(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
226 |         } else {
227 |           /*
228 |            * We want to traverse in reverse order because we want the LAST
229 |            * definition in the sub-tree....
230 |            * But we have no better way to traverse in reverse other :'(
231 |            */
232 |           for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getChildBefore(c)) {
233 |             computeMayUse(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
234 |           }
235 |         }
236 |     }
237 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }

920 |         Node maybeExpr = n.getFirstChild();
921 |         if (maybeExpr.isExprResult()) {
922 |           // IE has a bug where event handlers behave differently when
923 |           // their return value is used vs. when their return value is in
924 |           // an EXPR_RESULT. It's pretty freaking weird. See:

/**
     * Replace the provide statement.
     *
     * If we're providing a name with no definition, then create one.
     * If we're providing a name with a duplicate definition, then make sure
     * that definition becomes a declaration.
     */
Method code:
890 |     void replace() {
891 |       if (firstNode == null) {
892 |         // Don't touch the base case ('goog').
893 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
894 |         return;
895 |       }
896 |

898 |       // provided symbol.
899 |       if (candidateDefinition != null && explicitNode != null) {
900 |         explicitNode.detachFromParent();
901 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
902 | 
903 |         // Does this need a VAR keyword?
904 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
905 |         if (candidateDefinition.isExprResult() &&
906 |             !candidateDefinition.getFirstChild().isQualifiedName()) {

912 |             Node valueNode = nameNode.getNext();

927 |         replacementNode = createDeclarationNode();

929 |           firstNode.getParent().addChildBefore(replacementNode, firstNode);
930 |         } else {

932 |           // modules. We need to move this code up to a common module.

Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!n.isExprResult() && !n.isVar()) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (forVar.isName()
85 |           && n.isVar() && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // OK, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.isFor()
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some JavaScript parsers (such
101 |       // as the PlayStation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (n.isVar()) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.StatementFusion.canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/StatementFusion.java
Original range: 46-83

Method code:
46 |   private static boolean canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
47 |     // Fold only statement block. NOT scripts block.
48 |     if (!block.isBlock()) {
49 |       return false;
50 |     }
51 | 
52 |     // Nothing to do here.
53 |     if (!block.hasChildren() || block.hasOneChild()) {
54 |       return false;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     Node last = block.getLastChild();
58 | 
59 |     for (Node c = block.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
60 |       if (!c.isExprResult() && c != last) {
61 |         return false;
62 |       }
63 |     }
64 | 
65 |     // TODO(user): Support more control statement for fusion.
66 |     // FOR
67 |     switch(last.getType()) {
68 |       case Token.IF:
69 |       case Token.THROW:
70 |       case Token.SWITCH:
71 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
72 |         return true;
73 |       case Token.RETURN:
74 |         // We don't want to add a new return value.
75 |         return last.hasChildren();
76 |       case Token.FOR:
77 |         return NodeUtil.isForIn(last) &&
78 |             // Avoid cases where we have for(var x = foo() in a) { ....
79 |             !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(last.getFirstChild());
80 |     }
81 | 
82 |     return false;
83 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ShadowVariables.GatherReferenceInfo.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ShadowVariables.java
Original range: 129-169
Documentation:

Method code:
129 |     @Override
130 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
131 |       // Skipping over non-name nodes and empty function names.
132 |       if (!NodeUtil.isReferenceName(n)) {
133 |         return;
134 |       }
135 | 
136 |       // We focus on shadowing local variables as their name occurs much more
137 |       // than global names.
138 |       // TODO(user): Alternatively, we could experiment with using a local
139 |       // name to shadow a global variable.
140 |       if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
141 |         return;
142 |       }
143 | 
144 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
145 |       if (var == null) {
146 |         // extern name or undefined name.
147 |         return;
148 |       }
149 | 
150 |       if (var.getScope().isGlobal()) {
151 |         // We will not shadow a global variable name.
152 |         return;
153 |       }
154 | 
155 |       // Using the definition of upward referencing, fill in the map.
156 |       if (var.getScope() != t.getScope()) {
157 |         for (Scope s = t.getScope();
158 |             s != var.getScope() && s.isLocal(); s = s.getParent()) {
159 |           scopeUpRefMap.put(s.getRootNode(), var.name);
160 |         }
161 |       }
162 | 
163 |       if (var.getScope() == t.getScope()) {
164 |         scopeUpRefMap.put(t.getScopeRoot(), var.name);
165 |       }
166 | 
167 |       // Find in the usage map that tracks a var and all of its usage.
168 |       varToNameUsage.put(var, n);
169 |     }

194 |     private void doInlinesForScope(NodeTraversal t, ReferenceMap referenceMap) {
195 |

216 |           // inlining heuristics. See InlineConstantsTest.

   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node

Method code:
124 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.VAR:
127 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
128 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
129 |              child != null;) {
130 |           Node next = child.getNext();
131 |           declareVar(child);
132 |           child = next;
133 |         }
134 |         return;
135 | 
136 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
138 |           return;
139 |         }
140 | 
141 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
142 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
143 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
144 |           return;

147 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
148 |

150 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().isName());
152 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child

155 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();

160 |         return;  // only one child to scan

162 |       case Token.SCRIPT:

164 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);

===== M0985 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeCondition(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 1120-1300
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to minimize conditions expressions, as there are additional
   * assumptions that can be made when it is known that the final result
   * is a boolean.
   *
   * The following transformations are done recursively:
   *   !(x||y) --> !x&&!y
   *   !(x&&y) --> !x||!y
   *   !!x     --> x
   * Thus:
   *   !(x&&!y) --> !x||!!y --> !x||y
   *
   *   Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made
   */
Method code:
1120 |   private Node tryMinimizeCondition(Node n) {
1121 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
1122 | 
1123 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1124 |       case Token.NOT:
1125 |         Node first = n.getFirstChild();
1126 |         switch (first.getType()) {
1127 |           case Token.NOT: {
1128 |               Node newRoot = first.removeFirstChild();
1129 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1130 |               reportCodeChange();
1131 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1132 |               // NOT children are handled below.
1133 |               return newRoot;
1134 |             }
1135 |           case Token.AND:
1136 |           case Token.OR: {
1137 |               // !(!x && !y) --> x || y
1138 |               // !(!x || !y) --> x && y
1139 |               // !(!x && y) --> x || !y
1140 |               // !(!x || y) --> x && !y
1141 |               // !(x && !y) --> !x || y
1142 |               // !(x || !y) --> !x && y
1143 |               // !(x && y) --> !x || !y
1144 |               // !(x || y) --> !x && !y
1145 |               Node leftParent = first.getFirstChild();
1146 |               Node rightParent = first.getLastChild();
1147 |               Node left, right;
1148 | 
1149 |               // Check special case when such transformation cannot reduce
1150 |               // due to the added ()
1151 |               // It only occurs when both of expressions are not NOT expressions
1152 |               if (!leftParent.isNot()
1153 |                   && !rightParent.isNot()) {
1154 |                 // If an expression has higher precedence than && or ||,
1155 |                 // but lower precedence than NOT, an additional () is needed
1156 |                 // Thus we do not preceed
1157 |                 int op_precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType());
1158 |                 if ((isLowerPrecedence(leftParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1159 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(leftParent, op_precedence))
1160 |                     || (isLowerPrecedence(rightParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1161 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(rightParent, op_precedence))) {
1162 |                   return n;
1163 |                 }
1164 |               }
1165 | 
1166 |               if (leftParent.isNot()) {
1167 |                 left = leftParent.removeFirstChild();
1168 |               } else {
1169 |                 leftParent.detachFromParent();
1170 |                 left = IR.not(leftParent).srcref(leftParent);
1171 |               }
1172 |               if (rightParent.isNot()) {
1173 |                 right = rightParent.removeFirstChild();
1174 |               } else {
1175 |                 rightParent.detachFromParent();
1176 |                 right = IR.not(rightParent).srcref(rightParent);
1177 |               }
1178 | 
1179 |               int newOp = (first.isAnd()) ? Token.OR : Token.AND;
1180 |               Node newRoot = new Node(newOp, left, right);
1181 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1182 |               reportCodeChange();
1183 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1184 |               // AND and OR children below.
1185 |               return newRoot;
1186 |             }
1187 | 
1188 |            default:
1189 |              TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(first);
1190 |              if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1191 |                boolean result = nVal.not().toBoolean(true);
1192 |                int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1193 |                return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1194 |              }
1195 |         }
1196 |         // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the NOT
1197 |         // children in the general case in the main post-order traversal.
1198 |         return n;
1199 | 
1200 |       case Token.OR:
1201 |       case Token.AND: {
1202 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
1203 |         Node right = n.getLastChild();
1204 | 
1205 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1206 |         // the children, this can't be done in the general case.
1207 |         left = tryMinimizeCondition(left);
1208 |         right = tryMinimizeCondition(right);
1209 | 
1210 |         // Remove useless conditionals
1211 |         // Handle four cases:
1212 |         //   x || false --> x
1213 |         //   x || true  --> true
1214 |         //   x && true --> x
1215 |         //   x && false  --> false
1216 |         TernaryValue rightVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right);
1217 |         if (NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right) != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1218 |           int type = n.getType();
1219 |           Node replacement = null;
1220 |           boolean rval = rightVal.toBoolean(true);
1221 | 
1222 |           // (x || FALSE) => x
1223 |           // (x && TRUE) => x
1224 |           if (type == Token.OR && !rval ||
1225 |               type == Token.AND && rval) {
1226 |             replacement = left;
1227 |           } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1228 |             replacement = right;
1229 |           }
1230 | 
1231 |           if (replacement != null) {
1232 |             n.detachChildren();
1233 |             parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1234 |             reportCodeChange();
1235 |             return replacement;
1236 |           }
1237 |         }
1238 |         return n;
1239 |       }
1240 | 
1241 |       case Token.HOOK: {
1242 |         Node condition = n.getFirstChild();
1243 |         Node trueNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
1244 |         Node falseNode = n.getLastChild();
1245 | 
1246 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1247 |         // the result children, this can't be done in the general case.
1248 |         // The condition is handled in the general case in #optimizeSubtree
1249 |         trueNode = tryMinimizeCondition(trueNode);
1250 |         falseNode = tryMinimizeCondition(falseNode);
1251 | 
1252 |         // Handle four cases:
1253 |         //   x ? true : false --> x
1254 |         //   x ? false : true --> !x
1255 |         //   x ? true : y     --> x || y
1256 |         //   x ? y : false    --> x && y
1257 |         Node replacement = null;
1258 |         TernaryValue trueNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(trueNode);
1259 |         TernaryValue falseNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(falseNode);
1260 |         if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE
1261 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1262 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1263 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1264 |           replacement = condition;
1265 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE
1266 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1267 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1268 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1269 |           replacement = IR.not(condition);
1270 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1271 |           // Remove useless true case.
1272 |           n.detachChildren();
1273 |           replacement = IR.or(condition, falseNode);
1274 |         } else if (falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1275 |           // Remove useless false case
1276 |           n.detachChildren();
1277 |           replacement = IR.and(condition, trueNode);
1278 |         }
1279 | 
1280 |         if (replacement != null) {
1281 |           parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1282 |           n = replacement;
1283 |           reportCodeChange();
1284 |         }
1285 | 
1286 |         return n;
1287 |       }
1288 | 
1289 |       default:
1290 |         // while(true) --> while(1)
1291 |         TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(n);
1292 |         if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1293 |           boolean result = nVal.toBoolean(true);
1294 |           int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1295 |           return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1296 |         }
1297 |         // We can't do anything else currently.
1298 |         return n;
1299 |     }
1300 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 508-530
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An r-value in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
508 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
509 |       switch (n.getType()) {
510 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
511 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
512 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
513 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
514 |         case Token.OR:
515 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
516 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
517 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
518 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
519 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
520 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
521 |         case Token.HOOK:
522 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
523 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
524 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
525 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
526 |           Node third = second.getNext();
527 |           return getValueType(third);
528 |       }
529 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
530 |     }
