===== M1007 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(Node,Predicate<Node>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 2895-2959
Documentation:
/**
   * @param locals A predicate to apply to unknown local values.
   * @return Whether the node is known to be a value that is not a reference
   *     outside the expression scope.
   */
Method code:
2895 |   static boolean evaluatesToLocalValue(Node value, Predicate<Node> locals) {
2896 |     switch (value.getType()) {
2897 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
2898 |         // A result that is aliased by a non-local name, is the effectively the
2899 |         // same as returning a non-local name, but this doesn't matter if the
2900 |         // value is immutable.
2901 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value.getLastChild())
2902 |             || (locals.apply(value)
2903 |                 && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals));
2904 |       case Token.COMMA:
2905 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2906 |       case Token.AND:
2907 |       case Token.OR:
2908 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals)
2909 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2910 |       case Token.HOOK:
2911 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild().getNext(), locals)
2912 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2913 |       case Token.INC:
2914 |       case Token.DEC:
2915 |         if (value.getBooleanProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP)) {
2916 |           return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals);
2917 |         } else {
2918 |           return true;
2919 |         }
2920 |       case Token.THIS:
2921 |         return locals.apply(value);
2922 |       case Token.NAME:
2923 |         return isImmutableValue(value) || locals.apply(value);
2924 |       case Token.GETELEM:
2925 |       case Token.GETPROP:
2926 |         // There is no information about the locality of object properties.
2927 |         return locals.apply(value);
2928 |       case Token.CALL:
2929 |         return callHasLocalResult(value)
2930 |             || isToStringMethodCall(value)
2931 |             || locals.apply(value);
2932 |       case Token.NEW:
2933 |         return newHasLocalResult(value)
2934 |                || locals.apply(value);
2935 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
2936 |       case Token.REGEXP:
2937 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
2938 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
2939 |         // Literals objects with non-literal children are allowed.
2940 |         return true;
2941 |       case Token.DELPROP:
2942 |       case Token.IN:
2943 |         // TODO(johnlenz): should IN operator be included in #isSimpleOperator?
2944 |         return true;
2945 |       default:
2946 |         // Other op force a local value:
2947 |         //  x = '' + g (x is now an local string)
2948 |         //  x -= g (x is now an local number)
2949 |         if (isAssignmentOp(value)
2950 |             || isSimpleOperator(value)
2951 |             || isImmutableValue(value)) {
2952 |           return true;
2953 |         }
2954 | 
2955 |         throw new IllegalStateException(
2956 |             "Unexpected expression node" + value +
2957 |             "\n parent:" + value.getParent());
2958 |     }
2959 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getNameForObjLitKey(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 448-500
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the fully qualified name corresponding to an object literal key,
     * as long as it and its prefix property names are valid JavaScript
     * identifiers. The object literal may be nested inside of other object
     * literals.
     *
     * For example, if called with node {@code n} representing "z" in any of
     * the following expressions, the result would be "w.x.y.z":
     * <code> var w = {x: {y: {z: 0}}}; </code>
     * <code> w.x = {y: {z: 0}}; </code>
     * <code> w.x.y = {'a': 0, 'z': 0}; </code>
     *
     * @param n A child of an OBJLIT node
     * @return The global name, or null if {@code n} doesn't correspond to the
     *   key of an object literal that can be named
     */
Method code:
448 |     String getNameForObjLitKey(Node n) {
449 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
450 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isObjectLit());
451 | 
452 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
453 |       if (gramps == null) {
454 |         return null;
455 |       }
456 | 
457 |       Node greatGramps = gramps.getParent();
458 |       String name;
459 |       switch (gramps.getType()) {
460 |         case Token.NAME:
461 |           // VAR
462 |           //   NAME (gramps)
463 |           //     OBJLIT (parent)
464 |           //       STRING (n)
465 |           if (greatGramps == null || !greatGramps.isVar()) {
466 |             return null;
467 |           }
468 |           name = gramps.getString();
469 |           break;
470 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
471 |           // ASSIGN (gramps)
472 |           //   NAME|GETPROP
473 |           //   OBJLIT (parent)
474 |           //     STRING (n)
475 |           Node lvalue = gramps.getFirstChild();
476 |           name = lvalue.getQualifiedName();
477 |           break;
478 |         case Token.STRING_KEY:
479 |           // OBJLIT
480 |           //   STRING (gramps)
481 |           //     OBJLIT (parent)
482 |           //       STRING (n)
483 |           if (greatGramps != null &&
484 |               greatGramps.isObjectLit()) {
485 |             name = getNameForObjLitKey(gramps);
486 |           } else {
487 |             return null;
488 |           }
489 |           break;
490 |         default:
491 |           return null;
492 |       }
493 |       if (name != null) {
494 |         String key = n.getString();
495 |         if (TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key)) {
496 |           return name + '.' + key;
497 |         }
498 |       }
499 |       return null;
500 |     }

===== M1052 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 692-789
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
692 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
693 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
694 |     /*
695 |      * This is the case where:
696 |      *
697 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
698 |      * the script.
699 |      *
700 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
701 |      * the caller of the function.
702 |      *
703 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
704 |      * back to the caller of the function.
705 |      *
706 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
707 |      * asked to traverse.
708 |      *
709 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
710 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
711 |      */
712 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
713 |     if (parent == null || parent.isFunction() ||
714 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
715 |       return null;
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
719 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
720 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
721 |       case Token.IF:
722 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
723 |       case Token.CASE:
724 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
725 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
726 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
727 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
728 |           if (parent.getNext().isCase()) {
729 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
730 |           } else if (parent.getNext().isDefaultCase()) {
731 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
732 |           } else {
733 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
734 |           }
735 |         } else {
736 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
737 |         }
738 |         break;
739 |       case Token.FOR:
740 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
741 |           return parent;
742 |         } else {
743 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
744 |         }
745 |       case Token.WHILE:
746 |       case Token.DO:
747 |         return parent;
748 |       case Token.TRY:
749 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
750 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
751 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
752 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
753 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
754 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
755 |           }
756 |         // CATCH block.
757 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
758 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
759 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
760 |           } else {
761 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
762 |           }
763 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
764 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
765 |           if (cfa != null) {
766 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
767 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.UNCOND, finallyNode);
768 |             }
769 |           }
770 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
771 |         }
772 |     }
773 | 
774 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
775 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
776 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
777 | 
778 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
779 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.isFunction()) {
780 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
781 |     }
782 | 
783 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
784 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
785 |     } else {
786 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transferred up the AST.
787 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
788 |     }
789 |   }

/**
   * Gets the condition of an ON_TRUE / ON_FALSE CFG edge.
   * @param n a node with an outgoing conditional CFG edge

Original range: 660-705

Method code:
660 |   private void compileInternal() {
661 |     setProgress(0.0);
662 |     parse();
663 |     // 15 percent of the work is assumed to be for parsing (based on some
664 |     // minimal analysis on big JS projects, of course this depends on options)
665 |     setProgress(0.15);
666 |     if (hasErrors()) {
667 |       return;
668 |     }
669 | 
670 |     if (!precheck()) {
671 |       return;
672 |     }
673 | 
674 |     if (options.nameAnonymousFunctionsOnly) {
675 |       // TODO(nicksantos): Move this into an instrument() phase maybe?
676 |       check();
677 |       return;
678 |     }
679 | 
680 |     if (!options.skipAllPasses) {
681 |       check();
682 |       if (hasErrors()) {
683 |         return;
684 |       }
685 | 
686 |       if (options.isExternExportsEnabled()
687 |           || options.externExportsPath != null) {
688 |         externExports();
689 |       }
690 | 
691 |       // IDE-mode is defined to stop here, before the heavy rewriting begins.
692 |       if (!options.ideMode) {
693 |         optimize();
694 |       }
695 |     }
696 | 
697 |     if (options.recordFunctionInformation) {
698 |       recordFunctionInformation();
699 |     }
700 | 
701 |     if (options.devMode == DevMode.START_AND_END) {
702 |       runSanityCheck();
703 |     }
704 |     setProgress(1.0);
705 |   }

/**
     * Users may specify JS inputs via the legacy {@code --js} option, as well
     * as via additional arguments to the Closure Compiler. For example, it is
     * convenient to leverage the additional arguments feature when using the
     * Closure Compiler in combination with {@code find} and {@code xargs}:
     * <pre>
     * find MY_JS_SRC_DIR -name '*.js' \
     *     | xargs java -jar compiler.jar --manage_closure_dependencies
     * </pre>
     * The {@code find} command will produce a list of '*.js' source files in
     * the {@code MY_JS_SRC_DIR} directory while {@code xargs} will convert them
     * to a single, space-delimited set of arguments that are appended to the
     * {@code java} command to run the Compiler.
     * <p>
     * Note that it is important to use the
     * {@code --manage_closure_dependencies} option in this case because the
     * order produced by {@code find} is unlikely to be sorted correctly with
     * respect to {@code goog.provide()} and {@code goog.requires()}.
     */
Method code:
426 |     List<String> getJsFiles() {
427 |       List<String> allJsInputs = Lists.newArrayListWithCapacity(
428 |           js.size() + arguments.size());
429 |       allJsInputs.addAll(js);
430 |       allJsInputs.addAll(arguments);
431 |       return allJsInputs;
432 |     }

/**
   * Gets all the dependencies of the given roots. The inputs must be returned
   * in a stable order. In other words, if A comes before B, and A does not
   * transitively depend on B, then A must also come before B in the returned
   * list.
   *
   * @param sorted If true, get them in topologically sorted order. If false,
   *     get them in the original order they were passed to the compiler.
   */
Method code:
210 |   public List<INPUT> getDependenciesOf(List<INPUT> roots, boolean sorted) {
211 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(inputs.containsAll(roots));
212 |     Set<INPUT> included = Sets.newHashSet();
213 |     Deque<INPUT> worklist = new ArrayDeque<INPUT>(roots);
214 |     while (!worklist.isEmpty()) {
215 |       INPUT current = worklist.pop();
216 |       if (included.add(current)) {
217 |         for (String req : current.getRequires()) {
218 |           INPUT dep = provideMap.get(req);
219 |           if (dep != null) {
220 |             worklist.add(dep);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |     }
225 | 
226 |     ImmutableList.Builder<INPUT> builder = ImmutableList.builder();
227 |     for (INPUT current : (sorted ? sortedList : inputs)) {
228 |       if (included.contains(current)) {
229 |         builder.add(current);
230 |       }
231 |     }
232 |     return builder.build();
233 |   }

===== M1127 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

/**
   * Removes any vars in the scope that were not referenced. Removes any
   * assignments to those variables as well.
   */
Method code:
784 |   private void removeUnreferencedVars() {
785 |     CodingConvention convention = codingConvention;
786 | 
787 |     for (Iterator<Var> it = maybeUnreferenced.iterator(); it.hasNext(); ) {
788 |       Var var = it.next();
789 | 
790 |       // Remove calls to inheritance-defining functions where the unreferenced
791 |       // class is the subclass.
792 |       for (Node exprCallNode : inheritsCalls.get(var)) {
793 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(exprCallNode.getParent(), exprCallNode);
794 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
795 |       }
796 | 
797 |       // Regardless of what happens to the original declaration,
798 |       // we need to remove all assigns, because they may contain references
799 |       // to other unreferenced variables.
800 |       removeAllAssigns(var);
801 |

808 |           toRemove.isVar() ||
809 |           toRemove.isFunction() ||

813 |

831 |         // If this is a single var declaration, we can at least remove the
832 |         // declaration itself and just leave the value, e.g.,

835 |           parent.replaceChild(toRemove,

839 |       } else if (toRemove.isVar() &&

Documentation:
/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
830 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
831 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
832 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
833 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
834 |         if (handler.isFunction()) {
835 |           return;
836 |         }

839 | 
840 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
841 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
842 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
843 |           } else {
844 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
845 |           }
846 |         } else { // Has a catch.
847 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
848 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
849 |             return;
850 |           } else {
851 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
852 |           }
853 |         }
854 |         lastJump = handler;
855 |       }
856 |     }
857 |   }

     * Determines whether a set operation is a constructor or enumeration
     * declaration. The set operation may either be an assignment to a name,
     * a variable declaration, or an object literal key mapping.
     *
     * @param n The node that represents the name being set
     * @param parent Parent node of {@code n} (an ASSIGN, VAR, or OBJLIT node)
     * @return Whether the set operation is either a constructor or enum
     *     declaration

Method code:
577 |     private boolean isConstructorOrEnumDeclaration(Node n, Node parent) {
578 |       JSDocInfo info;
579 |       int valueNodeType;
580 |       switch (parent.getType()) {

582 |           info = parent.getJSDocInfo();

592 |           break;

595 |             info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
596 |             valueNodeType = Token.FUNCTION;
597 |             break;

599 |           return false;
600 |       }

   * BasicTypeExpression := '*' | 'null' | 'undefined' | TypeName
   *     | FunctionType | UnionType | RecordType | ArrayType
   */
Method code:
1730 |   private Node parseBasicTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1731 |     if (token == JsDocToken.STAR) {
1732 |       return newNode(Token.STAR);
1733 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.LB) {

1735 |       return parseArrayType(next());

1741 |       return parseUnionType(next());

1745 |         skipEOLs();

1748 |         return newStringNode(string);
1749 |       } else {

===== M1198 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 75-166
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries apply our various peephole minimizations on the passed in node.
   */
Method code:
75 |   @Override
76 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
77 |   public Node optimizeSubtree(Node node) {
78 |     switch(node.getType()) {
79 |       case Token.RETURN: {
80 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
81 |         if (result != node) {
82 |           return result;
83 |         }
84 |         result = tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
85 |         if (result != node) {
86 |           return result;
87 |         }
88 |         return tryReduceReturn(node);
89 |       }
90 | 
91 |       case Token.THROW: {
92 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
93 |         if (result != node) {
94 |           return result;
95 |         }
96 |         return tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
97 |       }
98 | 
99 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Maybe remove redundant BREAK and CONTINUE. Overlaps
100 |       // with MinimizeExitPoints.
101 | 
102 |       case Token.NOT:
103 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
104 |         return tryMinimizeNot(node);
105 | 
106 |       case Token.IF:
107 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
108 |         return tryMinimizeIf(node);
109 | 
110 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
111 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
112 |         return node;
113 | 
114 |       case Token.HOOK:
115 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
116 |         return node;
117 | 
118 |       case Token.WHILE:
119 |       case Token.DO:
120 |         tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
121 |         return node;
122 | 
123 |       case Token.FOR:
124 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(node)) {
125 |           tryJoinForCondition(node);
126 |           tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
127 |         }
128 |         return node;
129 | 
130 |       case Token.TRUE:
131 |       case Token.FALSE:
132 |         return reduceTrueFalse(node);
133 | 
134 |       case Token.NEW:
135 |         node = tryFoldStandardConstructors(node);
136 |         if (!node.isCall()) {
137 |           return node;
138 |         }
139 |         // Fall through on purpose because tryFoldStandardConstructors() may
140 |         // convert a NEW node into a CALL node
141 |       case Token.CALL:
142 |         Node result =  tryFoldLiteralConstructor(node);
143 |         if (result == node) {
144 |           result = tryFoldSimpleFunctionCall(node);
145 |           if (result == node) {
146 |             result = tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(node);
147 |           }
148 |         }
149 |         return result;
150 | 
151 |       case Token.COMMA:
152 |         return trySplitComma(node);
153 | 
154 |       case Token.NAME:
155 |         return tryReplaceUndefined(node);
156 | 
157 |       case Token.BLOCK:
158 |         return tryReplaceIf(node);
159 | 
160 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
161 |         return tryMinimizeArrayLiteral(node);
162 | 
163 |       default:
164 |         return node; //Nothing changed
165 |     }
166 |   }

240 |   void addNumber(double x) {
241 |     // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of x- -4 as
242 |     // x--4 (which is a syntax error).
243 |     char prev = getLastChar();
244 |     boolean negativeZero = isNegativeZero(x);
245 |     if ((x < 0 || negativeZero) && prev == '-') {
246 |       add(" ");

248 |

253 |       if (Math.abs(x) >= 100) {

255 |           mantissa /= 10;
256 |           exp++;
257 |         }
258 |       }
259 |       if (exp > 2) {

261 |       } else {
262 |         addConstant(Long.toString(value));
263 |       }
264 |     } else {

266 |     }
267 |   }

336 |   protected int getChar() {
337 |     if (ungetCursor != 0) {
338 |       cursor++;
339 |       --ungetCursor;
340 |       if (charno == -1) {
341 |         charno = getOffset();
342 |       }
343 |       return ungetBuffer[ungetCursor];
344 |     }
345 | 
346 |     for(;;) {
347 |       int c;
348 |       if (sourceCursor == sourceEnd) {
349 |         hitEOF = true;
350 |         if (charno == -1) {
351 |           charno = getOffset();
352 |         }
353 |         return EOF_CHAR;
354 |       }
355 |       cursor++;
356 |       c = sourceString.charAt(sourceCursor++);
357 | 
358 | 
359 |       if (lineEndChar >= 0) {
360 |         if (lineEndChar == '\r' && c == '\n') {
361 |           lineEndChar = '\n';
362 |           continue;
363 |         }
364 |         lineEndChar = -1;
365 |         lineStart = sourceCursor - 1;
366 |         lineno++;
367 |       }
368 | 
369 |       if (c <= 127) {
370 |         if (c == '\n' || c == '\r') {
371 |           lineEndChar = c;
372 |           c = '\n';
373 |         }
374 |       } else {
375 |         if (isJSFormatChar(c)) {
376 |           continue;
377 |         }
378 |         if (ScriptRuntime.isJSLineTerminator(c)) {
379 |           lineEndChar = c;
380 |           c = '\n';
381 |         }
382 |       }
383 | 
384 |       if (charno == -1) {
385 |         charno = getOffset();
386 |       }
387 | 
388 |       return c;
389 |     }
390 |   }

914 |       if (value.indexOf('\u000B') != -1) {
915 |         // NOTE(nicksantos): In JavaScript, there are 3 ways to
916 |         // represent a vertical tab: \v, \x0B, \u000B.
917 |         // The \v notation was added later, and is not understood
918 |         // on IE. So we need to preserve it as-is. This is really
919 |         // obnoxious, because we do not have a good way to represent
920 |         // how the original string was encoded without making the

922 |         //

/**
     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
     * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.
     */
Method code:
640 |     private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {
641 |       Preconditions.checkState(
642 |           functionBody.getParent().isFunction());
643 |       Node previous = null;
644 |       Node current = functionBody.getFirstChild();
645 |       // Skip any declarations at the beginning of the function body, they
646 |       // are already in the right place.

648 |         previous = current;

666 |         } else {

668 |           previous = current;

989 |   static boolean functionCallHasSideEffects(

991 |     if (!callNode.isCall()) {

994 |     }

1002 |     // Built-in functions with no side effects.

1006 |         return false;

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.UnionTypeBuilder.addAlternate(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/UnionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 121-212
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
121 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
122 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
123 |     // just bail out early here.
124 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
125 |       return this;
126 |     }
127 | 
128 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
129 | 
130 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
131 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
132 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
133 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
134 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
135 |     }
136 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
137 |       if (alternate.isUnionType()) {
138 |         UnionType union = alternate.toMaybeUnionType();
139 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
140 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
141 |         }
142 |       } else {
143 |         if (alternates.size() > maxUnionSize) {
144 |           return this;
145 |         }
146 | 
147 |         // Function types are special, because they have their
148 |         // own bizarro sub-lattice. See the commants on
149 |         // FunctionType#supAndInf helper and above at functionTypePosition.
150 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType() && functionTypePosition != -1) {
151 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
152 |           FunctionType other =
153 |               alternates.get(functionTypePosition).toMaybeFunctionType();
154 |           FunctionType supremum =
155 |               alternate.toMaybeFunctionType().supAndInfHelper(other, true);
156 |           alternates.set(functionTypePosition, supremum);
157 |           result = null;
158 |           return this;
159 |         }
160 | 
161 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
162 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
163 |         // one another.
164 |         int currentIndex = 0;
165 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
166 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
167 |           JSType current = it.next();
168 | 
169 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
170 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
171 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
172 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
173 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
174 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
175 |               current.isNoResolvedType()) {
176 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
177 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
178 |               return this;
179 |             }
180 |           } else {
181 |             if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
182 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
183 |               return this;
184 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
185 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
186 |               it.remove();
187 | 
188 |               if (currentIndex == functionTypePosition) {
189 |                 functionTypePosition = -1;
190 |               } else if (currentIndex < functionTypePosition) {
191 |                 functionTypePosition--;
192 |                 currentIndex--;
193 |               }
194 |             }
195 |           }
196 |           currentIndex++;
197 |         }
198 | 
199 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType()) {
200 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
201 |           Preconditions.checkState(functionTypePosition == -1);
202 |           functionTypePosition = alternates.size();
203 |         }
204 | 
205 |         alternates.add(alternate);
206 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
207 |       }
208 |     } else {
209 |       result = null;
210 |     }
211 |     return this;
212 |   }

/**
   * TypeName := NameExpression | NameExpression TypeApplication
   * TypeApplication := '.<' TypeExpressionList '>'
   * TypeExpressionList := TypeExpression // a white lie
   */
Method code:
1763 |   private Node parseTypeName(JsDocToken token) {
1764 |     if (token != JsDocToken.STRING) {
1765 |       return reportGenericTypeSyntaxWarning();
1766 |     }
1767 | 
1768 |     String typeName = stream.getString();
1769 |     int lineno = stream.getLineno();
1770 |     int charno = stream.getCharno();
1771 |     while (match(JsDocToken.EOL) &&
1772 |         typeName.charAt(typeName.length() - 1) == '.') {
1773 |       skipEOLs();
1774 |       if (match(JsDocToken.STRING)) {
1775 |         next();
1776 |         typeName += stream.getString();
1777 |       }
1778 |     }
1779 | 
1780 |     Node typeNameNode = newStringNode(typeName, lineno, charno);
1781 | 
1782 |     if (match(JsDocToken.LT)) {
1783 |       next();
1784 |       skipEOLs();
1785 |       Node memberType = parseTypeExpressionList(next());
1786 |       if (memberType != null) {
1787 |         typeNameNode.addChildToFront(memberType);
1788 | 
1789 |         skipEOLs();
1790 |         if (!match(JsDocToken.GT)) {
1791 |           return reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.gt");
1792 |         }
1793 | 
1794 |         next();
1795 |       }
1796 |     }
1797 |     return typeNameNode;
1798 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ShadowVariables.DoShadowVariables.enterScope(NodeTraversal)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ShadowVariables.java
Original range: 175-226
Documentation:

Method code:
175 |     @Override
176 |     public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
177 |       Scope s = t.getScope();
178 |       if (!s.isLocal()) {
179 |         return;
180 |       }
181 | 
182 |       // Since we don't shadow global, there is nothing to be done in the
183 |       // first immediate local scope as well.
184 |       if (s.getParent().isGlobal()) {
185 |         return;
186 |       }
187 | 
188 |       for (Iterator<Var> vars = s.getVars(); vars.hasNext();) {
189 |         Var var = vars.next();
190 | 
191 |         // Don't shadow variables that is bleed-out to fix an IE bug.
192 |         if (var.isBleedingFunction()) {
193 |           continue;
194 |         }
195 | 
196 |         // Don't shadow an exported local.
197 |         if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.name, s.isLocal())) {
198 |           continue;
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         // Try to look for the best shadow for the current candidate.
202 |         Assignment bestShadow = findBestShadow(s, var);
203 |         if (bestShadow == null) {
204 |           continue;
205 |         }
206 | 
207 |         // The name assignment being shadowed.
208 |         Assignment localAssignment = assignments.get(var.getName());
209 | 
210 |         // Only shadow if this increases the number of occurrences of the
211 |         // shadowed variable.
212 |         if (bestShadow.count < localAssignment.count) {
213 |           continue; // Hope the next local variable would have a smaller count.
214 |         }
215 | 
216 |         doShadow(localAssignment, bestShadow, var);
217 | 
218 |         if (oldPseudoNameMap != null) {
219 |           String targetPseudoName =
220 |             oldPseudoNameMap.get(s.getVar(bestShadow.oldName).nameNode);
221 |           for (Node use : varToNameUsage.get(var)) {
222 |             deltaPseudoNameMap.put(use, targetPseudoName);
223 |           }
224 |         }
225 |       }
226 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.unrollBinaryOperator(Node,int,String,Context,Context,int,int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 741-757
Documentation:
/**
   * We could use addList recursively here, but sometimes we produce
   * very deeply nested operators and run out of stack space, so we
   * just unroll the recursion when possible.
   *
   * We assume nodes are left-recursive.
   */
Method code:
741 |   private void unrollBinaryOperator(
742 |       Node n, int op, String opStr, Context context,
743 |       Context rhsContext, int leftPrecedence, int rightPrecedence) {
744 |     Node firstNonOperator = n.getFirstChild();
745 |     while (firstNonOperator.getType() == op) {
746 |       firstNonOperator = firstNonOperator.getFirstChild();
747 |     }
748 | 
749 |     addExpr(firstNonOperator, leftPrecedence, context);
750 | 
751 |     Node current = firstNonOperator;
752 |     do {
753 |       current = current.getParent();
754 |       cc.addOp(opStr, true);
755 |       addExpr(current.getFirstChild().getNext(), rightPrecedence, rhsContext);
756 |     } while (current != n);
757 |   }

/**
   * @return Whether the Node is a DO or FUNCTION (with or without
   * labels).
   */
Method code:
861 |   private boolean isOneExactlyFunctionOrDo(Node n) {
862 |     if (n.isLabel()) {
863 |       Node labeledStatement = n.getLastChild();
864 |       if (!labeledStatement.isBlock()) {
865 |         return isOneExactlyFunctionOrDo(labeledStatement);
866 |       } else {
867 |         // For labels with block children, we need to ensure that a

===== M1384 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.add(Node,Context)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 85-732
Documentation:

Method code:
85 |   void add(Node n, Context context) {
86 |     if (!cc.continueProcessing()) {
87 |       return;
88 |     }
89 | 
90 |     int type = n.getType();
91 |     String opstr = NodeUtil.opToStr(type);
92 |     int childCount = n.getChildCount();
93 |     Node first = n.getFirstChild();
94 |     Node last = n.getLastChild();
95 | 
96 |     // Handle all binary operators
97 |     if (opstr != null && first != last) {
98 |       Preconditions.checkState(
99 |           childCount == 2,
100 |           "Bad binary operator \"%s\": expected 2 arguments but got %s",
101 |           opstr, childCount);
102 |       int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
103 | 
104 |       // For right-hand-side of operations, only pass context if it's
105 |       // the IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE one.
106 |       Context rhsContext = getContextForNoInOperator(context);
107 | 
108 |       // Handle associativity.
109 |       // e.g. if the parse tree is a * (b * c),
110 |       // we can simply generate a * b * c.
111 |       if (last.getType() == type &&
112 |           NodeUtil.isAssociative(type)) {
113 |         addExpr(first, p, context);
114 |         cc.addOp(opstr, true);
115 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
116 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(last)) {
117 |         // Assignments are the only right-associative binary operators
118 |         addExpr(first, p, context);
119 |         cc.addOp(opstr, true);
120 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
121 |       } else {
122 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, type, opstr, context, rhsContext, p, p + 1);
123 |       }
124 |       return;
125 |     }
126 | 
127 |     cc.startSourceMapping(n);
128 | 
129 |     switch (type) {
130 |       case Token.TRY: {
131 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getNext().isBlock() &&
132 |                 !first.getNext().hasMoreThanOneChild());
133 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount >= 2 && childCount <= 3);
134 | 
135 |         add("try");
136 |         add(first, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
137 | 
138 |         // second child contains the catch block, or nothing if there
139 |         // isn't a catch block
140 |         Node catchblock = first.getNext().getFirstChild();
141 |         if (catchblock != null) {
142 |           add(catchblock);
143 |         }
144 | 
145 |         if (childCount == 3) {
146 |           add("finally");
147 |           add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
148 |         }
149 |         break;
150 |       }
151 | 
152 |       case Token.CATCH:
153 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
154 |         add("catch(");
155 |         add(first);
156 |         add(")");
157 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
158 |         break;
159 | 
160 |       case Token.THROW:
161 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
162 |         add("throw");
163 |         add(first);
164 | 
165 |         // Must have a ';' after a throw statement, otherwise safari can't
166 |         // parse this.
167 |         cc.endStatement(true);
168 |         break;
169 | 
170 |       case Token.RETURN:
171 |         add("return");
172 |         if (childCount == 1) {
173 |           add(first);
174 |         } else {
175 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
176 |         }
177 |         cc.endStatement();
178 |         break;
179 | 
180 |       case Token.VAR:
181 |         if (first != null) {
182 |           add("var ");
183 |           addList(first, false, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
184 |         }
185 |         break;
186 | 
187 |       case Token.LABEL_NAME:
188 |         Preconditions.checkState(!n.getString().isEmpty());
189 |         addIdentifier(n.getString());
190 |         break;
191 | 
192 |       case Token.NAME:
193 |         if (first == null || first.isEmpty()) {
194 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
195 |         } else {
196 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
197 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
198 |           cc.addOp("=", true);
199 |           if (first.isComma()) {
200 |             addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.ASSIGN), Context.OTHER);
201 |           } else {
202 |             // Add expression, consider nearby code at lowest level of
203 |             // precedence.
204 |             addExpr(first, 0, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
205 |           }
206 |         }
207 |         break;
208 | 
209 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
210 |         add("[");
211 |         addArrayList(first);
212 |         add("]");
213 |         break;
214 | 
215 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
216 |         add("(");
217 |         addList(first);
218 |         add(")");
219 |         break;
220 | 
221 |       case Token.COMMA:
222 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
223 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, Token.COMMA, ",", context, Context.OTHER, 0, 0);
224 |         break;
225 | 
226 |       case Token.NUMBER:
227 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
228 |         cc.addNumber(n.getDouble());
229 |         break;
230 | 
231 |       case Token.TYPEOF:
232 |       case Token.VOID:
233 |       case Token.NOT:
234 |       case Token.BITNOT:
235 |       case Token.POS: {
236 |         // All of these unary operators are right-associative
237 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
238 |         cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
239 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
240 |         break;
241 |       }
242 | 
243 |       case Token.NEG: {
244 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
245 | 
246 |         // It's important to our sanity checker that the code
247 |         // we print produces the same AST as the code we parse back.
248 |         // NEG is a weird case because Rhino parses "- -2" as "2".
249 |         if (n.getFirstChild().isNumber()) {
250 |           cc.addNumber(-n.getFirstChild().getDouble());
251 |         } else {
252 |           cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
253 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
254 |         }
255 | 
256 |         break;
257 |       }
258 | 
259 |       case Token.HOOK: {
260 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
261 |         int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
262 |         addExpr(first, p + 1, context);
263 |         cc.addOp("?", true);
264 |         addExpr(first.getNext(), 1, Context.OTHER);
265 |         cc.addOp(":", true);
266 |         addExpr(last, 1, Context.OTHER);
267 |         break;
268 |       }
269 | 
270 |       case Token.REGEXP:
271 |         if (!first.isString() ||
272 |             !last.isString()) {
273 |           throw new Error("Expected children to be strings");
274 |         }
275 | 
276 |         String regexp = regexpEscape(first.getString(), outputCharsetEncoder);
277 | 
278 |         // I only use one .add because whitespace matters
279 |         if (childCount == 2) {
280 |           add(regexp + last.getString());
281 |         } else {
282 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
283 |           add(regexp);
284 |         }
285 |         break;
286 | 
287 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
288 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
289 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
290 |         }
291 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
292 |         boolean funcNeedsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
293 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
294 |           add("(");
295 |         }
296 | 
297 |         add("function");
298 |         add(first);
299 | 
300 |         add(first.getNext());
301 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
302 |         cc.endFunction(context == Context.STATEMENT);
303 | 
304 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
305 |           add(")");
306 |         }
307 |         break;
308 | 
309 |       case Token.GETTER_DEF:
310 |       case Token.SETTER_DEF:
311 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getParent().isObjectLit());
312 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
313 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.isFunction());
314 | 
315 |         // Get methods are unnamed
316 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getFirstChild().getString().isEmpty());
317 |         if (type == Token.GETTER_DEF) {
318 |           // Get methods have no parameters.
319 |           Preconditions.checkState(!first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasChildren());
320 |           add("get ");
321 |         } else {
322 |           // Set methods have one parameter.
323 |           Preconditions.checkState(first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasOneChild());
324 |           add("set ");
325 |         }
326 | 
327 |         // The name is on the GET or SET node.
328 |         String name = n.getString();
329 |         Node fn = first;
330 |         Node parameters = fn.getChildAtIndex(1);
331 |         Node body = fn.getLastChild();
332 | 
333 |         // Add the property name.
334 |         if (!n.isQuotedString() &&
335 |             TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(name) &&
336 |             // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that were
337 |             // Unicode escaped.
338 |             NodeUtil.isLatin(name)) {
339 |           add(name);
340 |         } else {
341 |           // Determine if the string is a simple number.
342 |           double d = getSimpleNumber(name);
343 |           if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
344 |             cc.addNumber(d);
345 |           } else {
346 |             addJsString(n);
347 |           }
348 |         }
349 | 
350 |         add(parameters);
351 |         add(body, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
352 |         break;
353 | 
354 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
355 |       case Token.BLOCK: {
356 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
357 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
358 |         }
359 |         boolean preserveBlock = context == Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK;
360 |         if (preserveBlock) {
361 |           cc.beginBlock();
362 |         }
363 | 
364 |         boolean preferLineBreaks =
365 |             type == Token.SCRIPT ||
366 |             (type == Token.BLOCK &&
367 |                 !preserveBlock &&
368 |                 n.getParent() != null &&
369 |                 n.getParent().isScript());
370 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
371 |           add(c, Context.STATEMENT);
372 | 
373 |           // VAR doesn't include ';' since it gets used in expressions
374 |           if (c.isVar()) {
375 |             cc.endStatement();
376 |           }
377 | 
378 |           if (c.isFunction()) {
379 |             cc.maybeLineBreak();
380 |           }
381 | 
382 |           // Prefer to break lines in between top-level statements
383 |           // because top-level statements are more homogeneous.
384 |           if (preferLineBreaks) {
385 |             cc.notePreferredLineBreak();
386 |           }
387 |         }
388 |         if (preserveBlock) {
389 |           cc.endBlock(cc.breakAfterBlockFor(n, context == Context.STATEMENT));
390 |         }
391 |         break;
392 |       }
393 | 
394 |       case Token.FOR:
395 |         if (childCount == 4) {
396 |           add("for(");
397 |           if (first.isVar()) {
398 |             add(first, Context.IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE);
399 |           } else {
400 |             addExpr(first, 0, Context.IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE);
401 |           }
402 |           add(";");
403 |           add(first.getNext());
404 |           add(";");
405 |           add(first.getNext().getNext());
406 |           add(")");
407 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
408 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
409 |         } else {
410 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
411 |           add("for(");
412 |           add(first);
413 |           add("in");
414 |           add(first.getNext());
415 |           add(")");
416 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
417 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
418 |         }
419 |         break;
420 | 
421 |       case Token.DO:
422 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
423 |         add("do");
424 |         addNonEmptyStatement(first, Context.OTHER, false);
425 |         add("while(");
426 |         add(last);
427 |         add(")");
428 |         cc.endStatement();
429 |         break;
430 | 
431 |       case Token.WHILE:
432 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
433 |         add("while(");
434 |         add(first);
435 |         add(")");
436 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
437 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
438 |         break;
439 | 
440 |       case Token.EMPTY:
441 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
442 |         break;
443 | 
444 |       case Token.GETPROP: {
445 |         Preconditions.checkState(
446 |             childCount == 2,
447 |             "Bad GETPROP: expected 2 children, but got %s", childCount);
448 |         Preconditions.checkState(
449 |             last.isString(),
450 |             "Bad GETPROP: RHS should be STRING");
451 |         boolean needsParens = (first.isNumber());
452 |         if (needsParens) {
453 |           add("(");
454 |         }
455 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
456 |         if (needsParens) {
457 |           add(")");
458 |         }
459 |         add(".");
460 |         addIdentifier(last.getString());
461 |         break;
462 |       }
463 | 
464 |       case Token.GETELEM:
465 |         Preconditions.checkState(
466 |             childCount == 2,
467 |             "Bad GETELEM: expected 2 children but got %s", childCount);
468 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
469 |         add("[");
470 |         add(first.getNext());
471 |         add("]");
472 |         break;
473 | 
474 |       case Token.WITH:
475 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
476 |         add("with(");
477 |         add(first);
478 |         add(")");
479 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
480 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
481 |         break;
482 | 
483 |       case Token.INC:
484 |       case Token.DEC: {
485 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
486 |         String o = type == Token.INC ? "++" : "--";
487 |         int postProp = n.getIntProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP);
488 |         // A non-zero post-prop value indicates a post inc/dec, default of zero
489 |         // is a pre-inc/dec.
490 |         if (postProp != 0) {
491 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
492 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
493 |         } else {
494 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
495 |           add(first);
496 |         }
497 |         break;
498 |       }
499 | 
500 |       case Token.CALL:
501 |         // We have two special cases here:
502 |         // 1) If the left hand side of the call is a direct reference to eval,
503 |         // then it must have a DIRECT_EVAL annotation. If it does not, then
504 |         // that means it was originally an indirect call to eval, and that
505 |         // indirectness must be preserved.
506 |         // 2) If the left hand side of the call is a property reference,
507 |         // then the call must not a FREE_CALL annotation. If it does, then
508 |         // that means it was originally an call without an explicit this and
509 |         // that must be preserved.
510 |         if (isIndirectEval(first)
511 |             || n.getBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL) && NodeUtil.isGet(first)) {
512 |           add("(0,");
513 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.COMMA), Context.OTHER);
514 |           add(")");
515 |         } else {
516 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
517 |         }
518 |         add("(");
519 |         addList(first.getNext());
520 |         add(")");
521 |         break;
522 | 
523 |       case Token.IF:
524 |         boolean hasElse = childCount == 3;
525 |         boolean ambiguousElseClause =
526 |             context == Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE && !hasElse;
527 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
528 |           cc.beginBlock();
529 |         }
530 | 
531 |         add("if(");
532 |         add(first);
533 |         add(")");
534 | 
535 |         if (hasElse) {
536 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
537 |               first.getNext(), Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE, false);
538 |           add("else");
539 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
540 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
541 |         } else {
542 |           addNonEmptyStatement(first.getNext(), Context.OTHER, false);
543 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
544 |         }
545 | 
546 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
547 |           cc.endBlock();
548 |         }
549 |         break;
550 | 
551 |       case Token.NULL:
552 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
553 |         cc.addConstant("null");
554 |         break;
555 | 
556 |       case Token.THIS:
557 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
558 |         add("this");
559 |         break;
560 | 
561 |       case Token.FALSE:
562 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
563 |         cc.addConstant("false");
564 |         break;
565 | 
566 |       case Token.TRUE:
567 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
568 |         cc.addConstant("true");
569 |         break;
570 | 
571 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
572 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
573 |         add("continue");
574 |         if (childCount == 1) {
575 |           if (!first.isLabelName()) {
576 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
577 |           }
578 |           add(" ");
579 |           add(first);
580 |         }
581 |         cc.endStatement();
582 |         break;
583 | 
584 |       case Token.DEBUGGER:
585 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
586 |         add("debugger");
587 |         cc.endStatement();
588 |         break;
589 | 
590 |       case Token.BREAK:
591 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
592 |         add("break");
593 |         if (childCount == 1) {
594 |           if (!first.isLabelName()) {
595 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
596 |           }
597 |           add(" ");
598 |           add(first);
599 |         }
600 |         cc.endStatement();
601 |         break;
602 | 
603 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
604 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
605 |         add(first, Context.START_OF_EXPR);
606 |         cc.endStatement();
607 |         break;
608 | 
609 |       case Token.NEW:
610 |         add("new ");
611 |         int precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
612 | 
613 |         // If the first child contains a CALL, then claim higher precedence
614 |         // to force parentheses. Otherwise, when parsed, NEW will bind to the
615 |         // first viable parentheses (don't traverse into functions).
616 |         if (NodeUtil.containsType(
617 |             first, Token.CALL, NodeUtil.MATCH_NOT_FUNCTION)) {
618 |           precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType()) + 1;
619 |         }
620 |         addExpr(first, precedence, Context.OTHER);
621 | 
622 |         // '()' is optional when no arguments are present
623 |         Node next = first.getNext();
624 |         if (next != null) {
625 |           add("(");
626 |           addList(next);
627 |           add(")");
628 |         }
629 |         break;
630 | 
631 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
632 |         Preconditions.checkState(
633 |             childCount == 1, "Object lit key must have 1 child");
634 |         addJsString(n);
635 |         break;
636 | 
637 |       case Token.STRING:
638 |         Preconditions.checkState(
639 |             childCount == 0, "A string may not have children");
640 |         addJsString(n);
641 |         break;
642 | 
643 |       case Token.DELPROP:
644 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
645 |         add("delete ");
646 |         add(first);
647 |         break;
648 | 
649 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
650 |         boolean needsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
651 |         if (needsParens) {
652 |           add("(");
653 |         }
654 |         add("{");
655 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
656 |           if (c != first) {
657 |             cc.listSeparator();
658 |           }
659 | 
660 |           if (c.isGetterDef() || c.isSetterDef()) {
661 |             add(c);
662 |           } else {
663 |             Preconditions.checkState(c.isStringKey());
664 |             String key = c.getString();
665 |             // Object literal property names don't have to be quoted if they
666 |             // are not JavaScript keywords
667 |             if (!c.isQuotedString() &&
668 |                 !TokenStream.isKeyword(key) &&
669 |                 TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key) &&
670 |                 // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that
671 |                 // were Unicode escaped.
672 |                 NodeUtil.isLatin(key)) {
673 |               add(key);
674 |             } else {
675 |               // Determine if the string is a simple number.
676 |               double d = getSimpleNumber(key);
677 |               if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
678 |                 cc.addNumber(d);
679 |               } else {
680 |                 addExpr(c, 1, Context.OTHER);
681 |               }
682 |             }
683 |             add(":");
684 |             addExpr(c.getFirstChild(), 1, Context.OTHER);
685 |           }
686 |         }
687 |         add("}");
688 |         if (needsParens) {
689 |           add(")");
690 |         }
691 |         break;
692 |       }
693 | 
694 |       case Token.SWITCH:
695 |         add("switch(");
696 |         add(first);
697 |         add(")");
698 |         cc.beginBlock();
699 |         addAllSiblings(first.getNext());
700 |         cc.endBlock(context == Context.STATEMENT);
701 |         break;
702 | 
703 |       case Token.CASE:
704 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
705 |         add("case ");
706 |         add(first);
707 |         addCaseBody(last);
708 |         break;
709 | 
710 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
711 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
712 |         add("default");
713 |         addCaseBody(first);
714 |         break;
715 | 
716 |       case Token.LABEL:
717 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
718 |         if (!first.isLabelName()) {
719 |           throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
720 |         }
721 |         add(first);
722 |         add(":");
723 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
724 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), true);
725 |         break;
726 | 
727 |       default:
728 |         throw new Error("Unknown type " + type + "\n" + n.toStringTree());
729 |     }
730 | 
731 |     cc.endSourceMapping(n);
732 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected(Node,Set<String>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1112-1144
Documentation:
/**
   * @param knownConstants A set of names known to be constant value at
   * node 'n' (such as locals that are last written before n can execute).
   * @return Whether the tree can be affected by side-effects or
   * has side-effects.
   */
Method code:
1112 |   static boolean canBeSideEffected(Node n, Set<String> knownConstants) {
1113 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1114 |       case Token.CALL:
1115 |       case Token.NEW:
1116 |         // Function calls or constructor can reference changed values.
1117 |         // TODO(johnlenz): Add some mechanism for determining that functions
1118 |         // are unaffected by side effects.
1119 |         return true;
1120 |       case Token.NAME:
1121 |         // Non-constant names values may have been changed.
1122 |         return !isConstantName(n)
1123 |             && !knownConstants.contains(n.getString());
1124 | 
1125 |       // Properties on constant NAMEs can still be side-effected.
1126 |       case Token.GETPROP:
1127 |       case Token.GETELEM:
1128 |         return true;
1129 | 
1130 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
1131 |         // Function expression are not changed by side-effects,
1132 |         // and function declarations are not part of expressions.
1133 |         Preconditions.checkState(isFunctionExpression(n));
1134 |         return false;
1135 |     }
1136 | 
1137 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
1138 |       if (canBeSideEffected(c, knownConstants)) {
1139 |         return true;
1140 |       }
1141 |     }
1142 | 
1143 |     return false;
1144 |   }

/**
   * Create a map of constant names to constant values from a textual
   * description of the map.
   *
   * @param definitions A list of overriding definitions for defines in
   *     the form <name>[=<val>], where <val> is a number, boolean, or
   *     single-quoted string without single quotes.
   */
Method code:
1289 |   @VisibleForTesting
1290 |   static void createDefineOrTweakReplacements(List<String> definitions,
1291 |       CompilerOptions options, boolean tweaks) {
1292 |     // Parse the definitions
1293 |     for (String override : definitions) {
1294 |       String[] assignment = override.split("=", 2);
1295 |       String defName = assignment[0];
1296 | 
1297 |       if (defName.length() > 0) {
1298 |         String defValue = assignment.length == 1 ? "true" : assignment[1];
1299 | 
1300 |         boolean isTrue = defValue.equals("true");
1301 |         boolean isFalse = defValue.equals("false");
1302 |         if (isTrue || isFalse) {
1303 |           if (tweaks) {
1304 |             options.setTweakToBooleanLiteral(defName, isTrue);
1305 |           } else {
1306 |             options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, isTrue);
1307 |           }
1308 |           continue;
1309 |         } else if (defValue.length() > 1
1310 |             && ((defValue.charAt(0) == '\'' &&
1311 |                 defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\'')
1312 |                 || (defValue.charAt(0) == '\"' &&
1313 |                     defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\"'))) {
1314 |           // If the value starts and ends with a single quote,
1315 |           // we assume that it's a string.
1316 |           String maybeStringVal =
1317 |               defValue.substring(1, defValue.length() - 1);
1318 |           if (maybeStringVal.indexOf(defValue.charAt(0)) == -1) {
1319 |             if (tweaks) {
1320 |               options.setTweakToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1321 |             } else {
1322 |               options.setDefineToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1323 |             }
1324 |             continue;
1325 |           }
1326 |         } else {
1327 |           try {
1328 |             double value = Double.parseDouble(defValue);
1329 |             if (tweaks) {
1330 |               options.setTweakToDoubleLiteral(defName, value);
1331 |             } else {
1332 |               options.setDefineToDoubleLiteral(defName, value);
1333 |             }
1334 |             continue;
1335 |           } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
1336 |             // do nothing, it will be caught at the end
1337 |           }
1338 |         }
1339 |       }
1340 | 
1341 |       if (tweaks) {
1342 |         throw new RuntimeException(
1343 |             "--tweak flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1344 |       }
1345 |       throw new RuntimeException(
1346 |           "--define flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1347 |     }
1348 |   }

52 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
53 |     GraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = t.getControlFlowGraph().getNode(n);
54 |     if (gNode != null && gNode.getAnnotation() != GraphReachability.REACHABLE) {
55 | 
56 |       // Only report error when there are some line number informations.
57 |       // There are synthetic nodes with no line number informations, nodes

62 |           !n.isEmpty() && !n.isBreak()) {

66 |         new GraphReachability<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>(
67 |             t.getControlFlowGraph()).recompute(n);
68 |

===== M1468 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.assignNames(Set<Assignment>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 441-511
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
441 |   private void assignNames(Set<Assignment> varsToRename) {
442 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
443 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
444 | 
445 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
446 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator =
447 |         prefix.isEmpty() ? globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(
448 |             reservedNames, "", reservedCharacters);
449 | 
450 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
451 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
452 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
453 | 
454 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
455 |       if (a.newName != null) {
456 |         continue;
457 |       }
458 | 
459 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
460 |         continue;
461 |       }
462 | 
463 |       String newName;
464 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
465 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
466 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
467 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
468 |       } else {
469 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
470 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
471 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
472 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
473 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
474 |       }
475 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
476 |     }
477 | 
478 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
479 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
480 |     // follows:
481 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
482 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
483 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
484 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
485 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
486 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
487 |     //    compressible.
488 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
489 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
490 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
491 | 
492 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
493 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
494 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
495 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
496 | 
497 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
498 |       // generated names of the same length.

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1683-1724
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1683 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1684 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1685 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1686 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1687 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1688 |       // {?} - right curly
1689 |       // {?=} - equals
1690 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1691 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1692 |       // {function(number, ...[?])} - right bracket
1693 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1694 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1695 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1696 |       token = next();
1697 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1698 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1699 |           token == JsDocToken.RB ||
1700 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1701 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1702 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE) {
1703 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1704 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1705 |       }
1706 | 
1707 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1708 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1709 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1710 |     } else {
1711 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1712 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1713 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1714 |           next();
1715 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1716 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1717 |           next();
1718 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1719 |         }
1720 |       }
1721 | 
1722 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1723 |     }
1724 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.FunctionType.setPrototype(ObjectType,Node)

/**
   * Sets the prototype.
   * @param prototype the prototype. If this value is {@code null} it will
   *        silently be discarded.
   */
Method code:
374 |   boolean setPrototype(ObjectType prototype, Node propertyNode) {
375 |     if (prototype == null) {
376 |       return false;
377 |     }
378 |     // getInstanceType fails if the function is not a constructor
379 |     if (isConstructor() && prototype == getInstanceType()) {
380 |       return false;
381 |     }
382 | 
383 |     ObjectType oldPrototype = prototypeSlot == null
384 |         ? null : (ObjectType) prototypeSlot.getType();
385 |     boolean replacedPrototype = oldPrototype != null;
386 | 
387 |     this.prototypeSlot = new Property("prototype", prototype, true,
388 |         propertyNode == null ? source : propertyNode);
389 |     prototype.setOwnerFunction(this);
390 | 
391 |     if (oldPrototype != null) {
392 |       // Disassociating the old prototype makes this easier to debug--
393 |       // we don't have to worry about two prototypes running around.
394 |       oldPrototype.setOwnerFunction(null);
395 |     }
396 | 
397 |     if (isConstructor() || isInterface()) {
398 |       FunctionType superClass = getSuperClassConstructor();
399 |       if (superClass != null) {
400 |         superClass.addSubType(this);
401 |       }
402 | 
403 |       if (isInterface()) {
404 |         for (ObjectType interfaceType : getExtendedInterfaces()) {
405 |           if (interfaceType.getConstructor() != null) {
406 |             interfaceType.getConstructor().addSubType(this);
407 |           }
408 |         }
409 |       }
410 |     }
411 | 
412 |     if (replacedPrototype) {
413 |       clearCachedValues();
414 |     }
415 | 
416 |     return true;
417 |   }

804 |     @Override
805 |     Node processObjectLiteral(ObjectLiteral literalNode) {
806 |       if (literalNode.isDestructuring()) {
807 |         reportDestructuringAssign(literalNode);
808 |       }
809 | 
810 |       Node node = newNode(Token.OBJECTLIT);
811 |       for (ObjectProperty el : literalNode.getElements()) {
812 |         if (config.languageMode == LanguageMode.ECMASCRIPT3) {
813 |           if (el.isGetter()) {
814 |             reportGetter(el);
815 |             continue;
816 |           } else if (el.isSetter()) {
817 |             reportSetter(el);
818 |             continue;

826 |         if (el.isGetter()) {
827 |           key.setType(Token.GETTER_DEF);
828 |           Preconditions.checkState(value.isFunction());
829 |           if (getFnParamNode(value).hasChildren()) {

835 |           if (!getFnParamNode(value).hasOneChild()) {
836 |             reportSetterParam(el.getLeft());
837 |           }
838 |         }
839 |         key.addChildToFront(value);
840 |         node.addChildToBack(key);
841 |       }
842 |       return node;
843 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
