Method code:
83 |   @Override
84 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
85 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
86 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
87 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
88 |     // so we'll allow it.
89 |     if (n.isEmpty() ||
90 |         n.isComma()) {
91 |       return;
92 |     }
93 | 
94 |     if (parent == null) {
95 |       return;
96 |     }
97 | 
98 |     int pt = parent.getType();
99 |     if (pt == Token.COMMA) {
100 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
101 |       if (gramps.isCall() &&
102 |           parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
103 |         // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
104 |         // call to an eval. See ECMA-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's OK for the first
105 |         // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
106 |         // an eval.
107 |         if (n == parent.getFirstChild() &&
108 |             parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
109 |             n.getNext().isName() &&
110 |             "eval".equals(n.getNext().getString())) {
111 |           return;
112 |         }
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       if (n == parent.getLastChild()) {
116 |         for (Node an : parent.getAncestors()) {
117 |           int ancestorType = an.getType();
118 |           if (ancestorType == Token.COMMA)
119 |             continue;
120 |           if (ancestorType != Token.EXPR_RESULT &&
121 |               ancestorType != Token.BLOCK)
122 |             return;
123 |           else
124 |             break;
125 |         }
126 |       }
127 |     } else if (pt != Token.EXPR_RESULT && pt != Token.BLOCK) {
128 |       if (pt == Token.FOR && parent.getChildCount() == 4 &&
129 |           (n == parent.getFirstChild() ||
130 |            n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext())) {
131 |         // Fall through and look for warnings for the 1st and 3rd child
132 |         // of a for.
133 |       } else {
134 |         return;  // it might be OK to not have a side-effect
135 |       }
136 |     }
137 | 
138 |     boolean isSimpleOp = NodeUtil.isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType());
139 |     if (isSimpleOp ||
140 |         !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n, t.getCompiler())) {
141 |       if (n.isQualifiedName() && n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
142 |         // This no-op statement was there so that JSDoc information could
143 |         // be attached to the name. This check should not complain about it.
144 |         return;
145 |       } else if (n.isExprResult()) {
146 |         // we already reported the problem when we visited the child.
147 |         return;
148 |       }
149 | 
150 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
151 |       if (n.isString()) {
152 |         msg = "Is there a missing '+' on the previous line?";
153 |       } else if (isSimpleOp) {
154 |         msg = "The result of the '" + Token.name(n.getType()).toLowerCase() +
155 |             "' operator is not being used.";
156 |       }
157 | 
158 |       t.getCompiler().report(
159 |           t.makeError(n, level, USELESS_CODE_ERROR, msg));
160 |       // TODO(johnlenz): determine if it is necessary to
161 |       // try to protect side-effect free statements as well.
162 |       if (!NodeUtil.isStatement(n)) {
163 |         problemNodes.add(n);
164 |       }
165 |     }
166 |   }

===== M1536 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 148-190
Documentation:

Method code:
148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.isFunction()) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

318 |     @Override
319 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {

322 |       }
323 | 
324 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() < 2) {
325 |         return;
326 |       }
327 | 
328 |       int type = n.getType();
329 |       Var aliasVar = null;
330 |       if (type == Token.NAME) {
331 |         String name = n.getString();
332 |         Var lexicalVar = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
333 |         if (lexicalVar != null && lexicalVar == aliases.get(name)) {
334 |           aliasVar = lexicalVar;
335 |         }
336 |       }
337 | 
338 |       // Validate the top-level of the goog.scope block.
339 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() == 2) {
340 |         if (aliasVar != null && NodeUtil.isLValue(n)) {
341 |           if (aliasVar.getNode() == n) {

349 |           }

354 |         } else if (type == Token.THIS) {

356 |         } else if (type == Token.THROW) {
357 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_THROW);
358 |         }

362 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() >= 2) {

368 |           // The node in aliasedNode (which is "g") will be replaced in the

207 |   private void applyCollapses() {
208 |     for (Collapse collapse : collapses) {
209 | 
210 |       Node var = new Node(Token.VAR);
211 |       var.copyInformationFrom(collapse.startNode);
212 |       collapse.parent.addChildBefore(var, collapse.startNode);
213 | 
214 |       boolean redeclaration = false;
215 |       for (Node n = collapse.startNode; n != collapse.endNode;) {
216 |         Node next = n.getNext();

219 |         collapse.parent.removeChildAfter(var);
220 |

228 |           Preconditions.checkState(lhs.isName());
229 |           Node rhs = assign.getLastChild();
230 |           lhs.addChildToBack(rhs.detachFromParent());
231 |           var.addChildToBack(lhs.detachFromParent());

233 |         }

235 |       }
236 |

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DependencyOptions.setMoocherDropping(boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DependencyOptions.java
Original range: 95-98
Documentation:
/**
   * Enables or disables moocher dropping mode.
   *
   * A 'moocher' is a file that does not provide any symbols (though they
   * may require symbols). This is usually because they don't want to
   * tie themselves to a particular dependency system (e.g., Closure's
   * goog.provide, CommonJS modules). So they rely on other people to
   * manage dependencies on them.
   *
   * If true, we drop these files when we prune dependencies.
   * If false, we always keep these files an anything they depend on.
   * The default is false.
   *
   * Notice that this option only makes sense if dependency pruning is on,
   * and a set of entry points is specified.
   *
   * @return this for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
95 |   public DependencyOptions setMoocherDropping(boolean enabled) {
96 |     this.dropMoochers = enabled;
97 |     return this;
98 |   }

1014 |   static boolean isSubtypeHelper(JSType thisType, JSType thatType) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(Node)

/**
   * @returns false iff the result of the expression is not consumed.
   */
Method code:
3090 |   static boolean isExpressionResultUsed(Node expr) {
3091 |     // TODO(johnlenz): consider sharing some code with trySimpleUnusedResult.
3092 |     Node parent = expr.getParent();
3093 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
3094 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
3095 |         return false;
3096 |       case Token.HOOK:

3102 |         return (expr == parent.getFirstChild())
3103 |             ? false : isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3104 |       case Token.FOR:
3105 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
3106 |           // Only an expression whose result is in the condition part of the
3107 |           // expression is used.
3108 |           return (parent.getChildAtIndex(1) == expr);
3109 |         }
3110 |         break;
3111 |     }
3112 |     return true;
3113 |   }

/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1905 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1906 |     return n.isFunction() && !isStatement(n);
1907 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.SortedDependencies.SortedDependencies(List<INPUT>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/SortedDependencies.java

Method code:
64 |   public SortedDependencies(List<INPUT> inputs)
65 |       throws CircularDependencyException {
66 |     this.inputs = Lists.newArrayList(inputs);
67 |     noProvides = Lists.newArrayList();
68 | 
69 |     // Collect all symbols provided in these files.
70 |     for (INPUT input : inputs) {
71 |       Collection<String> currentProvides = input.getProvides();
72 |       if (currentProvides.isEmpty()) {
73 |         noProvides.add(input);
74 |       }
75 | 
76 |       for (String provide : currentProvides) {
77 |         provideMap.put(provide, input);
78 |       }
79 |     }
80 | 
81 |     // Get the direct dependencies.
82 |     final Multimap<INPUT, INPUT> deps = HashMultimap.create();
83 |     for (INPUT input : inputs) {
84 |       for (String req : input.getRequires()) {
85 |         INPUT dep = provideMap.get(req);
86 |         if (dep != null && dep != input) {
87 |           deps.put(input, dep);
88 |         }
89 |       }
90 |     }
91 | 
92 |     // Sort the inputs by sucking in 0-in-degree nodes until we're done.
93 |     sortedList = topologicalStableSort(inputs, deps);
94 | 
95 |     // The dependency graph of inputs has a cycle iff sortedList is a proper
96 |     // subset of inputs. Also, it has a cycle iff the subgraph
97 |     // (inputs - sortedList) has a cycle. It's fairly easy to prove this
98 |     // by the lemma that a graph has a cycle iff it has a subgraph where
99 |     // no nodes have out-degree 0. I'll leave the proof of this as an exercise
100 |     // to the reader.
101 |     if (sortedList.size() < inputs.size()) {
102 |       List<INPUT> subGraph = Lists.newArrayList(inputs);
103 |       subGraph.removeAll(sortedList);
104 | 
105 |       throw new CircularDependencyException(
106 |           cycleToString(findCycle(subGraph, deps)));
107 |     }
108 |   }

/**
   * Look ahead for a type annotation by advancing the character stream.
   * Does not modify the token stream.
   * This is kind of a hack, and is only necessary because we use the token
   * stream to parse types, but need the underlying character stream to get
   * JsDoc descriptions.
   * @return Whether we found a type annotation.
   */
Method code:
2344 |   private boolean lookAheadForTypeAnnotation() {
2345 |     boolean matchedLc = false;
2346 |     int c;
2347 |     while (true) {
2348 |       c = stream.getChar();
2349 |       if (c == ' ') {
2350 |         continue;
2351 |       } else if (c == '{') {
2352 |         matchedLc = true;
2353 |         break;
2354 |       } else {
2355 |         break;
2356 |       }
2357 |     }
2358 |     stream.ungetChar(c);
2359 |     return matchedLc;
2360 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/VarCheck.java
Original range: 120-203

Method code:
120 |   @Override
121 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
122 |     if (!n.isName()) {
123 |       return;
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     String varName = n.getString();
127 | 
128 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
129 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
130 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent));
132 |       return;
133 |     }
134 | 
135 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
136 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
137 |     if ((parent.isVar() ||
138 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
139 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
140 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
141 | 
142 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
146 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
147 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
148 |     if (var == null) {
149 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
150 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
151 |         // current scope.
152 |       } else {
153 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
154 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
155 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
156 |         }
157 | 
158 |         if (sanityCheck) {
159 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
160 |         } else {
161 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
162 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
163 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
164 |         }
165 |       }
166 |       return;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
170 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
171 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
172 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
173 |       return;
174 |     }
175 | 
176 |     // Check module dependencies.
177 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
178 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
179 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
180 |     if (!sanityCheck &&
181 |         varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
182 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
183 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
184 |       } else {
185 |         if (scope.isGlobal()) {
186 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
187 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
188 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
189 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
190 |           } else {
191 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
192 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
193 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
194 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
195 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
196 |           }
197 |         } else {
198 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |         }
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }

286 |     @Override
287 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
288 |       RefInfo refInfo = allRefInfo.get(n);
289 |       if (refInfo != null) {
290 |         Ref ref = refInfo.ref;
291 |         Name name = refInfo.name;
292 |         String fullName = name.getFullName();
293 |         switch (ref.type) {
294 |           case SET_FROM_GLOBAL:
295 |           case SET_FROM_LOCAL:
296 |             Node valParent = getValueParent(ref);
297 |             Node val = valParent.getLastChild();
298 |             if (valParent.isAssign() && name.isSimpleName() &&
299 |                 name.getDeclaration() == ref) {
300 |               // For defines, it's an error if a simple name is assigned
301 |               // before it's declared
302 |               compiler.report(
303 |                   t.makeError(val, INVALID_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, fullName));
304 |             } else if (processDefineAssignment(t, fullName, val, valParent)) {
305 |               // remove the assignment so that the variable is still declared,
306 |               // but no longer assigned to a value, e.g.,
307 |               // DEF_FOO = 5; // becomes "5;"
308 | 
309 |               // We can't remove the ASSIGN/VAR when we're still visiting its
310 |               // children, so we'll have to come back later to remove it.
311 |               refInfo.name.removeRef(ref);
312 |               lvalueToRemoveLater = valParent;
313 |             }
314 |             break;
315 |           default:
316 |             if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
317 |               // Treat this as a reference to a define in the global scope.
318 |               // After this point, the define must not be reassigned,
319 |               // or it's an error.
320 |               DefineInfo info = assignableDefines.get(fullName);
321 |               if (info != null) {
322 |                 setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
323 |                 assignableDefines.remove(fullName);
324 |               }
325 |             }
326 |             break;
327 |         }
328 |       }
329 | 
330 |       if (!t.inGlobalScope() &&
331 |           n.getJSDocInfo() != null && n.getJSDocInfo().isDefine()) {
332 |         // warn about @define annotations in local scopes
333 |         compiler.report(
334 |             t.makeError(n, NON_GLOBAL_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, ""));
335 |       }
336 | 
337 |       if (lvalueToRemoveLater == n) {
338 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
339 |         if (n.isAssign()) {
340 |           Node last = n.getLastChild();
341 |           n.removeChild(last);
342 |           parent.replaceChild(n, last);
343 |         } else {
344 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.isName());
345 |           n.removeChild(n.getFirstChild());
346 |         }
347 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
348 |       }
349 |

351 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
352 |           // If there's a function call in the global scope,
353 |           // we just say it's unsafe and freeze all the defines.
354 |           //
355 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): We could be a lot smarter here. For example,
356 |           // ReplaceOverriddenVars keeps a call graph of all functions and
357 |           // which functions/variables that they reference, and tries
358 |           // to statically determine which functions are "safe" and which

   * Regenerates the provides/requires if we need to do so.
   */

205 |   private void regenerateDependencyInfoIfNecessary() throws IOException {
206 |     // If the code is NOT a JsAst, then it was not originally JS code.
207 |     // Look at the Ast for dependency info.
208 |     if (!(ast instanceof JsAst)) {
209 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(compiler,
210 |           "Expected setCompiler to be called first");
211 |       DepsFinder finder = new DepsFinder();
212 |       Node root = getAstRoot(compiler);
213 |       if (root == null) {

215 |       }
216 |

218 | 
219 |       // TODO(nicksantos|user): This caching behavior is a bit
220 |       // odd, and only works if you assume the exact call flow that

222 |       // getProvides(), then remove the goog.provide calls from the
223 |       // AST, and then call getProvides() again.
224 |       //

226 |       // compilation scheme. The API needs to be fixed so callers aren't
227 |       // doing weird things like this, and then we should get rid of the
228 |       // multiple-scan strategy.
229 |

   * Returns true if this is an immutable value.

Method code:
490 |   static boolean isImmutableValue(Node n) {
491 |     switch (n.getType()) {
492 |       case Token.STRING:
493 |       case Token.NUMBER:
494 |       case Token.NULL:
495 |       case Token.TRUE:
496 |       case Token.FALSE:
497 |         return true;
498 |       case Token.NOT:
499 |         return isImmutableValue(n.getFirstChild());
500 |       case Token.VOID:
501 |       case Token.NEG:
502 |         return isImmutableValue(n.getFirstChild());
503 |       case Token.NAME:
504 |         String name = n.getString();
505 |         // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
506 |         // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
507 |         return "undefined".equals(name)
508 |             || "Infinity".equals(name)
509 |             || "NaN".equals(name);
510 |     }
511 | 
512 |     return false;
513 |   }

===== M1632 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.collectObjectProperty(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.java
Original range: 228-261
Documentation:

Method code:
228 |   private boolean collectObjectProperty(
229 |       Node objectLiteral, Node propertyCandidate) {
230 |     Node assignment = propertyCandidate.getFirstChild();
231 |     Node lhs = assignment.getFirstChild(), rhs = lhs.getNext();
232 |     Node obj = lhs.getFirstChild();
233 |     Node property = obj.getNext();
234 | 
235 |     // The property must be statically known.
236 |     if (lhs.isGetElem()
237 |         && (!property.isString()
238 |             && !property.isNumber())) {
239 |       return false;
240 |     }
241 | 
242 |     String propertyName;
243 |     if (property.isNumber()) {
244 |       propertyName = NodeUtil.getStringValue(property);
245 |     } else {
246 |       propertyName = property.getString();
247 |     }
248 | 
249 |     Node newProperty = IR.stringKey(propertyName)
250 |         .copyInformationFrom(property);
251 |     // Preserve the quotedness of a property reference
252 |     if (lhs.isGetElem()) {
253 |       newProperty.setQuotedString();
254 |     }
255 |     Node newValue = rhs.detachFromParent();
256 |     newProperty.addChildToBack(newValue);
257 |     objectLiteral.addChildToBack(newProperty);
258 | 
259 |     propertyCandidate.detachFromParent();
260 |     return true;
261 |   }
